what: The battle effects recipe: every number an explosion, smoke, fire, tracer, muzzle flash and dust needs, for the preview clips and for the 3D game. The 3D game should read this file, not copy its numbers into code, so the effects can be tuned without a code change (as the sound mix's mix.json).
made: 2026-11-18, the effects artist, from the art director's sheet art-director/explosions/explosions-look.md (15:43Z), the sound mix sound/mix/mix.json and the tracer rule in tools/battle-models/airshow.py
units: metres, seconds, degrees. Frames are at 30 a second. Colours in [r, g, b] 0 to 255 are what the FINISHED picture should measure (the art director measures pixels), not shader inputs.

rulings.brian: 2026-11-18 15:39Z: 'i want the explosions to be very dramatic and life like... mimic this look and feel as much as possible'; 15:40Z: 'i love how it makes me feel like im in it and watching a movie at the same time'
rulings.own_design: The feeling only. Every effect, texture, sound and camera move is our own; nothing copied from any game (ruling 217, game-direction).
rulings.gore: None: no bodies torn apart (art director's default; Brian may rule otherwise).

burst._how: A high-explosive shell, mortar bomb, grenade or bomb landing on ground. Times are seconds after it lands (frame 0). Sizes scale by sizes.<kind>.scale (1 = 105 mm); the crown's height, crater, linger and shake come straight from the sizes table. On land the EARTH is the star: mostly thrown soil and smoke, almost no fire.

incoming._note: Played only where a real recording exists (mix.json impacts.incoming). Mortars a shorter flutter; tank and anti-tank guns none.

flash._ragged: Art director 19:57Z on build 1748's frames, where the flash was an even orange star, 202,124,6, darker than pale ground (214,196,166): a shell's flash follows the gun flashes' rule. With tongues here it is ragged and new every round: that many tongues of unequal length thrown mostly up and out as the dirt is, the longest reach_m (times the size's root scale), bright at the root and red-orange at the end; licks flung low; a lumpy orange body with a second lump to one side; a yellow inside it written yellow_over times white (lands 250,216,82, luma 214: over pale ground's 198, blue under 110); and a heart heart_share of the flash's width written over times white (lands 253,248,226). It lasts life_s, about two frames, shrinking and dense: the tongues stand among the first dirt, the body, yellow and heart shine through it. Art director 20:12Z: every edge fades out over feather_m (2 to 3 pixels from the battle eye) and no piece is one flat colour. Colours are WRITTEN values (picture._how). Without tongues: the old seven-pointed star in core_colour.
flash._soft: Art director 06:08Z 20 November on build 1758's frames. From 18 m feather_m is about one pixel and the tongues read as cut paper: every feathered edge now fades over at least feather_px pixels on the screen, whatever the distance. And in the game the tongues read as one flat orange (median green over red 0.50): each tongue's root is now yellow-orange (root_yellow of the way from orange to yellow; it lands about 243,202,63, green over red 0.8) from the body out to root_reach of what shows of the tongue, then turns orange and reddens to its tip (in the preview the flames' green over red runs 0.37 to 0.84, median 0.53 to 0.70). Neither key: as before.
flash._melt: Art director 08:03Z 20 November on build 1762's frames from 18 m: the root showed as a flat yellow petal with a firm line round it inside each orange tongue, and the flash read as a flower. With root_melt each tongue is drawn from the point where it leaves the body (root_from of what the body hides of it): orange there, running evenly out to the red-orange of its edge. Its root is the tongue's own shape laid over it, outline for outline, yellow and whole at that same point and thinning evenly to nothing at the tongue's rim, half gone root_melt of the way out and turning orange as it thins. So the yellow melts into the orange along the tongue and across it with no line anywhere, the hottest yellow runs down the centre line, and the edges are orange to red-orange. Heart, body, sizes, timing and dice are as they were. No root_melt: build 1762's root.

light._rule: a real light on the men, vehicles and ground within the radius; lifts the lower third of the frame 1.1 to 1.3x, never a white-out; checked by measuring the frame against the one before
light._passed: The fortifications 105 mm burst passed 17:11Z with its lamp 16 m up: ground lifted 1.24x at 3 m, 1.19x at 10 m, 1.12x at 15 m, a tank's side 1.10x at 28 m, gone by frame 3. Height scales by the square root of the size's scale. (Its second, low lamp that lit only the men and the tank is left out: the game has two lamps for all the flashes.)

flash._dusk: At dusk and night the flash lights the young smoke from inside for 3 or 4 frames: the most cinematic moment we have.
flash._core: Not a pale heart: yellow, blue channel under 110 (the fortifications burst passed 17:11Z with the pale heart at frame 0 left for the kit to fix).

ember._what: What the flash leaves low in the earth: a dull orange glow no wider than 'share' of the flash, dying to dark ('to') over life_s (art director 19:58Z 21 November: at most a third of the flash's width, 0.15 to 0.3 s).

skirt._shade: how strongly the skirt is lit on top and shadowed at its foot (1 is every other puff), so it shows its height (art director 17:09Z)
skirt._mend_1931: Art director 19:31Z: the skirt must be one low continuous haze, never puffs. Its pieces are now drawn as low flattened balls seen from where the eye is (a low wall from the side, the whole round they cover from above, where they used to be thin upright cards that read as separate dabs), larger, more of them, softer and fainter, so they run together.
skirt._budget: Fewer, larger pieces since they cover their whole round from above (19:45Z): 130 a 105 where 250 overflowed the room in a battery's salvo (the pre-check's count).
skirt._mend_0319: Art director 03:13Z (Brian's battle clips): from a low eye the skirt was a big flat beige pancake that veiled the crown's foot. Cut to reach 9 m, alpha 0.22 to 0.3; its rim broken into lobes (5 to 7, of uneven reach, never less than lobe_least of the reach between them); its outer feather share of the reach fading to a sixth, each piece soft from its middle out (heart 0); its top under most_high_m (times the square root of scale), rising only rise_mps as it hazes. Pass: no visible rim from a 1.7 m eye.

shock_ring.grass: flattens outward, springs back over 0.6 s
shock_ring._note: One continuous low skirt in the ground's own dust colour, racing out and thinning (art director 16:31Z), with height and a soft billowing top, settling to a low haze by frame 30 (16:53Z). Neighbours overlap by about half; each puff is an upright card, long along the ring, so its foot never cuts into the ground.
shock_ring._why_085: the skirt's tops face the sun and the ground is seen edge-on, so the ground's own dust drawn at full brightness reads paler than the ground; 0.85 matches it
shock_ring._ground_skirt: Art director 19:58Z 21 November: a low ring of dust rolls outward along the ground to 1.5 times the cloud's width over 1 to 2 s, stays low, and hangs with the cloud. of_cloud: the skirt's width across as that many times the size's cloud_m (the metres below are for a reach of roll_ref_m, a 105's, and go by the reach). skirt.hangs: it stays as long as the cloud, going as the cloud goes by the size's own linger times, never climbing; it keeps hang_keep times the cloud's share of its pieces, and widens and spreads hang_wide and hang_spread as much as the cloud's puffs do.

body._note: A dense dark mound of earth and dust at the crown's foot from frame 4, so the hit has weight; it slumps into the smoke.

foot_glow._art_director: 22:24Z (dusk salvo sheet): a flash's edge stays at about 180,75,35 or a warmer grey, never fully saturated; was 184,100,3. It dies to a warm grey ember (66,36,22), not a pure red.

crown.then: collapses into the smoke and rains back as a veil
crown._note: A wide torn fan (about 100 degrees) thrown outward from the point (art director 16:31Z and 16:53Z): a few heavy dark jets, very uneven in length and width, overlapping and bunched, never spaced like fingers; the gaps filled with lighter dust (fill_jets) so the silhouette is one torn fan; each heavy jet thinnest and torn at its tip, drawn to a point (tip_point), never rounded, with clods flying on beyond it (tip_clod_speed); a dense dark body at the foot from frame 4. Jet thickness is a share of the crown's height (jet_foot_r, jet_tip_r) and puffs are stepped along a jet by their own length (overlap), so a bomb's jets do not bead.
crown.azimuth: random round the compass, never evenly spaced: jets overlap and bunch
crown._edges: edge_jitter: how far each puff along a jet strays sideways, as a share of the jet's width; lump_chance: how many puffs are lumps half again or twice as wide. Ragged, clumpy sides, never smooth blades or leaves (art director 17:09Z).
crown._edge_rough: Each jet puff's outline is lumpy by this share (fill jets 0.6 of it), so a jet's sides are clumpy, never a smooth blade, with no more puffs.
crown._root: Art director 19:43Z: earth flying up is heavy at the root and thins only near the tip, with side edges broken as the clods are. Up to root_solid of a heavy jet's length its puffs are denser, and at each step a dense lumpy clump bulges out of its side (side_clumps is the chance).
crown._side_clump_rim: Art director 14:09Z (clods sheet, 1.0 s): the clumps bulging from a jet's root read as hard straight-cut polygons, the cut-card look, solid to a rim at 0.55 of their opacity with straight sides between the ring's points. As the heavy pieces were mended (_tips_1943), a clump keeps its dark heart out to the jet's inner ring and fades to side_clump_rim at its very edge, so its lumpy outline shows soft and no straight cut. Absent: 0.55, as before.
crown._tips_1943: Art director 19:43Z: jet sides read as glass shards or blades. The cause was each big heavy piece's wide see-through band (solid only to half its radius, then thinning to a hard rim), drawn with straight sides between the ring's points. Now a heavy piece is solid out to heavy_inner of its radius (heavy_heart) and fades in a thin soft edge with no rim, so its lumpy outline shows and nothing is glassy. The root stays dense and dark up to root_solid with clumps bulging from its sides (side_clumps); the tip is torn into smaller, rougher, scattered pieces (tip_grain, tip_rough, tip_inner), drawn out and pointed less (tip_stretch 1.2, tip_point 0.45). The lighter dust between the jets is scattered wider, lumpy and soft, never pointed (fill_scatter, fill_rough, fill_stretch).
crown._heavy_jets_0319: Art director 03:13Z (Brian's battle clips): 24 to 40 thin dark spiky jets in place of 5 to 8 heavy ones. The shells keep 3 to 5 heavy jets for the mass and add the spikes (burst.crown.spikes); the bombs keep their own passed fan (sizes.<bomb>.crown).

spikes._how: Thin dark rays of earth among the heavy jets: count of them (halved past burst.debris.shower.halve_past puffs), each a few lumps (pieces) along its length with small gaps (each lump lump_share of its place), edges broken by rough (foot to tip), drawn to a point, reaching reach times the crown's height, leaning lean times half the fan, thick times the jet's foot and tip radius, the heavy colour times shade, alpha falling to tip_alpha at the tip, a lump of tip_clod_m (times the square root of scale) riding each tip. The debris shower streams along them too. droop: the outer lumps fall faster (gravity up to 1 + droop at the tip), so the tip bends down after about 0.3 s. longest_of_median: no spike longer than this times the middle one (a long lone blade reads as a stick). stretch_most: no lump drawn longer than this times its width. Art director 03:28Z.

crown._streaks: Art director 03:27Z 22 November: at half a second the crown was 'a few broad flat wedges with straight edges... cardboard slabs. Keep the mass, but make it more, narrower streaks with soft tips that fall back by about 1.5 s.' So more heavy jets, each thinner (heavy_jets, heavy_thick); heavy_stretch: a heavy jet's pieces drawn that long for their width and stepped as far apart, so a thin jet is a streak of few pieces; heavy_swell: they widen that much over their lives and no more; heavy_droop: a piece falls faster the further up its jet (gravity up to 1 + heavy_droop at the tip), so the tips come back down; tip_life_s: how long the piece at the very tip lasts, the root's as ever; tip_heart, tip_alpha, tip_inner: a soft end. A size may have its own of each. The thin jets are paid for in pieces: fewer clumps on a jet's side, one or two clods off each tip, fewer spikes of fewer lumps, fewer fill jets and foot lumps, so a 105 holds about as many pieces as before (1,104 against 1,037 at most, and a barrage holds fewer).

foot._how: Art director 03:13Z, from Brian's battle clips: close-hit black is 29% of the burst in the clips and 0.8% in ours; the burst itself has to carry the black, no grade can. A dense mass of near-black lumps at the crown's base (and the crown's body near-black with it): count lumps (times the square root of scale, at least 0.7), out to width and up to height times the crown's height, each lump_r times the crown's height, the heavy colour times shade (near black), lit on top and dark below by light, lumpy by rough, living life_s and settling toward the smoke's colour mixed with settle_dust of the dust, settle of the way by its end, so near-black for 0.3 to 1.0 s, then brown-grey. Not on water. Pass: at 0.4 s on earth, at least 15% of the burst box under luma 60. The earth veil over the foot is the dust mixed veil_dark toward the heavy colour, and the smoke puffs in the lower smoke_band of the cloud start smoke_dark as bright, settling to the cloud's own colour by smoke_settle_s. The dust between the jets is the heavy colour mixed with fill_dust of its usual dust share, settling the same way.
foot._rim: Art director 14:09Z (clods sheet, 1.0 s): the burst's dark body beside and below its core showed hard straight-cut edges. A foot piece keeps its dark heart out to 0.7 of its radius and fades to rim (0.3 before) at its very edge, so the body's lumpy outline shows soft and its darkness is kept (the burst's mean level the same to a tenth). Absent: 0.3, as before.

clods._passed: With the clods thrown from the jets' tips, about 130 in all for a 105, landing 0.9 to 3.1 s after the flash, the big ones bouncing once (the fortifications burst, passed 17:11Z).
clods._chunk: Irregular chunks, never smooth beans (art director 19:36Z): each clod has its own lumpy outline (rough), tumbles as it flies, and has a lit face toward the sun and a dark one away (shade).
clods._most_long: Art director on cut 5 (06, 22 November): a fast clod drawn as a streak along its flight was a long dark slab across the men. A thrown lump (clod, shower, lens piece, a gun's kicked dirt; never a spark, an ember or a tracer) is drawn no longer than most_long times its width. Absent or 0: as before.

lens._rim: Art director 14:09Z (clods sheet, 1.0 s): the big dark lumps beside and below the burst, the pieces thrown past the lens, were hard straight-cut polygons, the cut-card look: solid to a rim at 0.6 of their opacity, with straight sides between the ring's points. Each keeps its dark heart out to inner of its radius and fades to rim at its very edge, so its torn outline shows soft. Absent: as before.
lens._rule: on a hit close to the camera a few clods and a veil of grit cross the foreground: what puts the player in the hole

debris._note: True gravity sells weight: a clod thrown 10 m up comes down about 2.8 s later.

shower._why: Brian's battle video (11-19): what makes a hit read as violent is a dense spray of dark lumps flung higher than the crown and twice as wide, raining back for one to three seconds. Ours threw a few small clods low. The shower: count lumps for a 105 (times the ground's shower share, default its clods share, and the shell's size squared up to most_k2), thrown up_mps and out_mps (both times the fourth root of the shell's scale, so a 105 tops out at 2 to 13 m and lands 1.2 to 3.3 s later), radius r_m (times the square root of scale; small_skew keeps most small), darkened by shade (backlit undersides), resting rest_s on the ground, a landing puff only from landing_puff_r_m. Water throws none. along_jets of them stream along the crown's jets (each within jet_spread of its way, at jet_speed times the speed that carries a lump to that jet's tip, so some fall short inside it and some fly on past), the rest flung every way at up_mps and out_mps.
shower._halve: Art director 03:13Z: with more than halve_past puffs live when a shell lands, it throws half the shower and half the spikes.

debris._dust_trails: Art director 19:58Z 21 November: dark clods tumble and fall back within 2 to 3 s (sizes.<size>.clods_back_s), a few trailing thin dust: dust_trails of the clods over dust_trail_from_m in radius (for a 105; by the size) shed a thin line of dust along their flight.

smoke.build: many small puffs, never a few big balls; volumes in the preview renders
smoke.merge: neighbours overlap; sizes vary 1 to 3 times; soft rims, no firm cores: never separate round balls like grapes (art director 16:53Z)
smoke._top: Warm brown near the ground, charcoal grey toward the top: brown all the way up reads as dust (art director 19:36Z). Each puff mixes toward colour_top by its height in the cloud, up to top_share.
smoke._cloud: Art director 19:43Z: the cloud's sunward side about 15 to 20 levels lighter than its shadow side, and its top broken into 3 to 5 lumps, not one smooth dome. cloud_shade lights or shadows each puff by where it sits in its cloud (as game.shade_lit and shade_dark), fully beyond cloud_r of the crown's height from the cloud's leaning middle; top_lobes gathers the upper puffs into a few lumps. Preview, 105 on earth at frame 40, sun from the side: the sunward third about 15 levels lighter than the shadow third once the cloud's own thinner downwind side is taken off (about 13 by halves).

scar.overlap: craters overlap where hits overlap: a barrage ploughs a green field

bulk._what: A burst with bulk (Brian, 18:30Z 21 November: 'the explosions should be bigger and more more realistic'; the art director's ruling of 19:58Z, art-director/explosions/smoke-burst-fire-ruling-r2.md): more bulk, a denser core and a longer hang, never a ball of soft smoke lifting off the ground. Where a size has cloud_m, its cloud is a column of the ground's own dark earth standing on the hit, many puffs at every height, hiding what is behind it through its first two seconds, in lighter grey-brown smoke and dust that is cloud_m across at the ground by about two seconds. It climbs from its foot and stays on the ground. Remove this row, or a size's cloud_m, and that cloud is the old one.
bulk._how: column: 'puffs' of them (more for a bigger burst), in a stack 'wide' of cloud_m across at the ground and top_wide of that at its top, 'tall' of the crown high; each puff_r of cloud_m in radius, as thick as 'alpha', its outline 'rough'; the top stands by climb_s and rises on at rise_mps, the foot not at all; 'soil' and 'shade' its colour between the ground's heavy earth and its soil, going 'settle' of the way to the settled brown-grey over life_s. fringe: 'puffs' of lighter smoke, 'tall' of the crown high, 'taper' narrower at its top than at the ground, rolling out to its place over roll_s.

throw._what: A shell's thrown earth at its flash (art director 03:27Z 22 November, on the bigger bursts: 'the throw at the flash is near black... a black comic-book splat with an orange dot. Make it dark earth brown with the faces toward the flash lit warm, floor about 15'). lighter and body: the jets, the spikes, the body and the foot are made lighter than the ground's heavy earth has them, until its brightest channel is the written value body (75 lands about 50), never more than lighter times: so they have a lit side and a shaded one above the floor, and sand or rubble, light already, stay as they are. mottle: each piece that share lighter or darker than the next, by its own lump seed, so a jet is streaked earth and never one flat fill. floor: no point of the jets, the spikes, the body, the foot or the column of earth is drawn darker than this, in the hour's light. flash_lit: how far the earth nearest the flash goes toward flash_colour on its side toward the flash as it goes off, dying to nothing over flash_lit_s; half as much flash_lit_reach of the flash's own width from it. A piece the eye sees from the flash's side is lit all over, one standing in front of it only on its edge. Not on water. Both colours are written values, aimed through the game's curve (picture._how): the floor lands about 40,33,26, 16 on the art director's scale of 100; flash_colour lands about 180,117,58. Remove the row and the throw is as it was.

far._how: The production lead's FX3 (battle-scale plan, 22 November): a hit on land outside a sea battle keeps a share of its pieces, each as much bigger. The share is FarK, its crown's height in the picture (crown_m, at the scene's own window pixels) against full_px, all of them at that or taller and never under least, times BusyK: with more than halve_past pieces asked for on the screen half, with the room four fifths full a quarter, with more asked than the room over_busy; a hit whole in the picture only near_busy, and only with the room four fifths full; between, by how small it stands. Of the crown it keeps every heavy jet, each of fewer pieces up to three times as long; the square root of the share of the dust between the jets, the body and the foot (each bigger); the share of the spikes, clumps and thrown clods. Its skirt keeps the share to skirt_pow, its smoke to smoke_pow, so a cloud seen after a cut to a nearer eye is softer but whole. And a piece of a land hit past gone_beyond_m that stands under gone_px across at its biggest, and a crater's mark likewise, takes no place in the room and is not laid (its flash never; its thrown dirt only with gone_dirt 1). A see-through piece of such a hit (skirt, smoke, the cloud's lighter fringe) laid Bigger times as wide is as thick as Bigger to alpha_pow of them laid one over another, never over alpha_most (the art director 12:33Z: with fewer layers the grass showed through the far clouds and tinted them; 0 or no key: as laid). Measured on the ground scene's whole-army wide shot (1,080 x 670, a 1.5 km front from 810 m back and 470 m up, the kit's crater marks off as the ground scene has them), 6 shells a second: the room asked 18,400 against 3,000 before and 3,200 now, Draw 7.9 ms before and 3.5 now on the test box (median of 3), and over four frames 96 of 101 young bursts show in the picture against 35 before (the bursts' own pieces filled the room and it left the farthest out first); 7.6 a second, 147 of 153 against 37, Draw 10.9 and 4.7 ms. A single burst at the preview's own distance is drawn as before, byte for byte. No row: as before.

sizes._how: Rough figures, already about 1.3 times real so they read at the battle camera (art director). Check in the scene against a known-size fitting: a man, 1.75 m. scale is for the puff and clod counts and sizes; shake is camera shake within shake_within_m. spout_m: the height of the white water column a hit in the sea throws (grounds.water.spout), where crown_m is the land burst's earth: the bigger land bursts of 22 November (crown_m raised) left the sea as it was, the pre-check 05:48Z; without it the sea takes crown_m.

torpedo._what: a torpedo against a ship's side (the scene passes this size for it; a kit without the row draws a field gun's burst, so pass it only with this recipe). On water: the tallest, narrowest column, over the mast, dark for its lower third.

churn._what: white water round a ship that is settling, going down or rolling over (the scene passes this size for it, on water only): no explosion, so quiet 1, no flash and no jolt. A low boil several times wider than it is tall (art director 22:03Z: the first was a white hedgehog mound): domes of pale water heaving up a few metres and sinking back, no two at the same moment, froth breaking round the foot of each, darker water between them, a burst of spray here and there as air vents, and a wide patch of foam that lasts. dome_in_s: each dome's water comes up out of the sea over that long, never all at once (the pre-check measured the patch's ink rising a sixth in one frame as a dome was born; art director 23:19Z: ease it in over about 0.3 s).

grounds._how: The ground under the hit decides the look. thrown is the crown's colour against the ground's own (or a fixed colour where given); smoke tints the cloud. The 3D field's ground kinds (open, field, woods, rough, marsh, water, road, bridge, buildings, rock, bunker, works, blown) map to these by ground_of (the game keeps its own table: a word it does not pass is never drawn).

sand.extra: pale, tall, slow dust cloud; glows when backlit
sand.core: darker damp sand in the heavy jets, inside the pale slow column, so it reads as a hit
sand._shower: A shell in sand still throws stones and damp lumps high (the video's beach): shower 0.8, though its clods share stays 0.15.

snow.crater: a black star on white with a grey-brown spatter ring
snow.extra: white snow thrown up first, dark earth under it
snow._mend_1931: Art director 19:31Z on the first in-game frames: the snow crown was smooth pure-white blades like a paper flower, ringed by cotton puffs. Now broken and granular (grain: its pieces half the size, twice as many, soft-edged, not drawn out), off-white (about 188,193,201 in shade; each grain its own shade) with dark earth showing in the jets (first_share: a third of the pieces snow at the jet's foot, four fifths at its tip).

mud.clod_kind: wet clumps that splash, not spray
mud.crater: black-brown spatter, water shining in it
mud.ground_shine: matt: wet earth, not a glaze

wet._how: The art director's read of the thaw (23 November, ground stills ca6aeca3; passed 01:19Z with the mends below): thrown mud is dark wet clods that land and stay, never a dust puff. Its own switch: on 0 (from 23 November) draws mud's burst as before; on 1, the clods and the shower take clod (the shower by shower_shade; land_grade.grounds.mud.wet.clod in the land battle, 42,39,37: a lying clump from 25 m a median of about 55,49,43 against the field's 78,68,54, dark wet grey-brown, never a black hole), the clods r_k as big (clumps, not spray); none bounces, none sheds dust in flight, none puffs dust where it lands; and of a burst within stay_within_m of the eye, up to stay_most clods of stay_from_m radius or more lie stay_s where they land, fading over the last fade_s. Farther bursts' clods go as before, after their short rest: a clod there is a pixel or two. spout._how: A hit in the sea (art director 17:54Z 20 November, from build 1778: the columns were soft white billows that hung like steam or cotton). With this row a shell, bomb or torpedo in the water throws white water and nothing else: a column up to the size's crown_m in about rise_s (a 50 m one; a small splash sooner), wide of its height at its stalk and crown_wide at its head. Its body stands to three quarters of the height; the top is fingers that rise inside it and bend out of its head (fingers of them, leaning finger_lean_deg at their tips, the tallest to the full height, the next clearly shorter, the rest finger_reach of it), each drawn to a torn point. Streamers of spray leave their heads (streamers a finger) and the column's sides (side_spray): each streamer_pieces pieces thrown one after another out to streamer_out of the column's height, so it is an arc that bends over under its own weight, thicker at its root and breaking into beads at its tip, and is gone before the column's top is down (art director 22:03Z: single streaks were dead-straight hairlines like a firework, and hung over the column like rain). The water goes up as a jet, each piece jet_stretch as long as it is wide (1.9 to 2.8 unless given), and comes down as a curtain, drawn out longer as it falls, the top back on the sea in fall_s. Its lowest base_to is dark wet water (base_colour) that breaks white above, with a low heave of the same round its foot (foot). The side away from the sun is shaded toward shadow by side_shade. A low ring of spray races out over the sea (surge) to foam_reach of the height; foam lies where it stood in a soft mottled patch (foam pieces, foam_alpha, gone in foam_s); a thin mist (mist puffs of mist_alpha, mist_s) goes off down the wind. body: the column's pieces, none bigger than piece_max_m. A small splash is fewer and coarser pieces by its height, and so is a hit far off: so far that a 50 m column would stand under full_px tall in the picture (the scene's window pixels), it has that share of its pieces, never under far_least, each as much bigger. smoke_bank._how: Art director 03:30Z 20 November (build 1750, Pearl Harbor from the air; Akagi in picture 06): the smoke resting on the sea beside a big fire was a smooth, soft dark oval with no lumps and no edge, a stain or a hole in the water. A fire from_m across or more lays its smoke as a bank of the oil column's own kind of lumps (rough, heart, twin_px, its sunward lumps lit toward lit_colour by sun_side), run out down the wind. The bank: its lumps wander wide times the fire's width apart by the far end and it is long times that in length; measured from straight above it comes to 2.2 to 2.9 times as long as it is wide. Each lump is lump_r of the fire's width in radius, is born on the fire every every_s (while it flames, after) and runs down the wind at the pace that takes the longest lived (life_s, for a 40 m fire; a 12 m fire's about half) to the far end. All live through the first short share of that, piling into one dark mass at the fire; fewer and fewer live on (thin: higher, fewer), each solid for hold of its life, so down the wind the bank thins to lumps apart with clear sea between. Most lie on the sea (rise_mps, rest) and keep the fire's dark (smoke_foot), each its own shade; heads of them lift (head_rise_mps) and pale as they ride clear. A young lump is lit only sun_young as much until sun_from of the longest life and in full by sun_by of it (art director 04:06Z: the dark pile at the root, the first third, takes about a tenth of the light and lands near the passed foot, luma about 32 and near neutral, reading by its edge against the sea; the light comes in through the middle so the far lumps keep their lit tops). Every dial is held to a sane span in the code. No such key, or a fire under from_m (a tank, a house): the old smoke, unchanged.

smoke_column._how: A big fire's own column (art director 04:06Z 20 November: a burning ship gets a column of her own, of the oil column's kind but about half its width: black at the root, lumps, leaning down the wind, rising a few hundred metres before it bends flat; the bank lies on the sea beneath it). A plain fire (Burn) from_m across or more that burns from_s seconds or longer sends one up: the oil column's own puffs and pall (the keys below are the oil row's, read the same way, sizes as shares of the fire's width), laid from this row. from_s: a shorter fire sends up none (a crashed aeroplane's 90 seconds lays its bank only). One column to a ship: a fire lit within join_m of a place a standing column rises from joins it; the column then rises from both fires and from between them (eight places at most; a fire that joins after that adds none, so a ship struck again and again keeps her one column), stands on their middle, and is join_wide of her burning length across (the fires' greatest distance apart plus the new fire's width; never wider than a fire join_m across would send up), so a carrier ablaze from end to end sends up one broad column and never three chimneys. most: so many columns stand at once and never more (each is some 95 to 130 puffs that are kept when the screen is full, as an oil column's are); a fire past that lays its bank only, chosen as it is lit and never by the eye. under_oil: none of it is laid while burning oil (OilFire) stands within this share of that oil's reach of one of her fires: the game lights an oil fire 0.6 of her length across on every ship lost, and that oil's column is hers. A column that oil has stood over does not stand again when the oil goes out, and takes no place among the most; a fire lit under burning oil starts none. 0: laid all the same. sun_young, sun_from_s, sun_by_s: a puff has only sun_young of its lit side until sun_from_s seconds old and all of it by sun_by_s, so the column is black at its root and its lit lumps come in higher up (any oil row can ask the same; none asked: as before). After the flames the column thins, greys and comes half as often until the fire ends. No fire.smoke_column.column_life_s key: no column, every fire as before.
smoke_column._tight: A small fire's column held in one piece (art director 15:40Z 20 November on the outcome looks' first cuts: 'at 300 m the ship fire's smoke breaks into a scatter of separate flakes. Each puff should overlap the next at every distance, at least 1.5 times the spacing with a floor in pixels'). A puff's size goes by the fire's width, but the scatter the row's spread of windage and push gives two puffs does not: over a 12 m fire the puffs were a fifth as wide as over a 60 m one and thrown as far apart. tight_m: a fire narrower than this keeps only its share (its width over tight_m) of that spread, so its puffs go nearly one way; at this width or wider nothing is changed (three fires along Akagi make a column 55 m wide: Midway 06 is laid as passed). overlap: under tight_m each puff is at least this many times as wide as the way to the next one, young and old, with what scatter is left. least_px, least_keep: far off a puff of the column is never under this many window pixels across, keeping that share of its ink. put_out._how: A fire its crew puts out (art director 14:39Z 20 November; BurnOut on a fire lit with a number): 'the smoke turns white, then the fire is gone'. over_s: seconds in which the flames are eaten back from the edges to the seat, lower and in fits, never thinner, when the caller gives none. surge_s: with water (a ship's hoses) white steam surges at the seat that long as it hits (the steam.surge row); with an extinguisher (a tank's crew) a brief pale puff instead. pale_s: by then the smoke has gone from black through grey to grey-white; it thins to a wisp and is gone gone_s after the crew began. The flames shrink steadily, half their height by two fifths of that time, never all gone and back. Where it burned a dull patch (glow, glow_alpha) lies on the seat and small specks flicker over it, embers of them alight at once at first and fewer to the end, embers_s after the last flame (art director 16:41Z: never round red lamps). No such row: BurnOut does nothing.

tongues._how: A burning thing's flames (Burn). Art director 17:54Z 20 November, from build 1778's ships: the fires were rows of pointed orange cones like birthday candles. With this row a fire burns at seats of its own (seats of them, fixed on the skin where it was lit, standing apart round its middle). Each seat throws ragged tongues tall of the fire's width high, each seat its own share of that so no two are the same height, one the tallest and more of them short (a fire over tall_wide_m across is less tall for its width); a tongue is wide of the width at its root, lives life_s and dies by being eaten away from below. A seat's height surges and sinks by pulse several times a second, no two seats together. A tongue leans lean for each metre a second of wind, lean_most at the most, and bends further over toward its tip. forks of them have a thinner tongue out of the same root leaning aside, and tips of them a thin tip above the body, so a flame's top is torn and never one point. Colour (art director 23:19Z: each flame was one flat orange from root to tip): a tongue is body at its root, running out to orange and then to tip, a dull deep red, at its edge and its top, and it reddens as it dies; its thin tip is that red, going darker. Under the tongues each seat keeps a bed that never goes out while the fire burns: a broad yellow foot where the flame leaves the skin, and along it, across the eye's line, two short blunt licks of root, white-yellow, burning root_over past white under the tallest seat and less under the rest (picture.lit_gain), so the heart of the fire is a ragged bright band along its foot and never a disc. foot_soft: the share of a lick, from its root out to its rim, over which it fades away (0.4 without the key; the art director 23:51Z: soften the licks a little so they do not read as cut shapes up close). torn: the chance a step (every_s) of a scrap torn off a tall tongue's top: ragged, blunt, dull red going to the smoke's dark, gone in a quarter of a second within a tongue's height (the first were darts flying across the smoke, which read as sparks). over_smoke: the fire's flames are sorted this share of its width nearer the eye, so its far seats show through its own smoke and are not blacked out by it (from a ship's distance they were). A fire under full_px wide in the picture (the scene's window pixels) burns at that share of its seats, never under seats_least, each as much wider, with as much fewer forks, tips and torn tips; and one under far_px wide stands taller, up to far_tall more, so far off it reads as fire before smoke. As the room fills a fire keeps its bed and its tongues' bodies and loses the forks, tips and torn tips, by degrees from seven tenths full to none at seventeen twentieths. Put out, it is eaten back to its middle, steadily lower and at fewer seats. Without this row: one or two upright cones a step, anywhere on the fire.

land_tongues._smooth: Smooth flames (the frame study of 22 November: each tongue was born whole on a step of a twentieth of a second and only shrank, so at 30 frames a second the fire popped ten times a second, 53% of its flicker over 8 Hz; with these keys 1%). born_k: a piece is born that share of its size and grows to it by full_by of its life, fading in over fade_in of it; jitter: born up to that share of a step late, so births never beat with the frames; anchor: its root stays on the seat; climb: how much of its old climb it keeps; bed_overlap: the foot lives that many times longer, so a seat's foot pieces cross-fade. flicker, flicker_long, flicker_wide: every piece of a seat swells and dims together by the clock, three smooth waves between flicker_hz (the ruling's 3 to 6 Hz), in strength, length and width. point and long_most: how pointed a tongue is drawn (0.9 before) and how long for its width at the most (5 before); lower, the fire reads as a heap of overlapping lobes and not a row of blades. The body (the ruling: 'one merged body of overlapping camera-facing flame puffs'): mass soft round flame puffs a step rise through it from the seats, mass_r of its width, mass_up of a seat's height their climb, mass_colour going to mass_top as they rise, so the flames go dark red into the smoke; soot black puffs a step roll off its top, soot_r of its width. Both thin out as the fire is small in the picture (to a quarter) and with the room near full (to half), each bigger to cover the same. bed: the foot's own colour in place of the fire's yellow-white heart (the ruling: orange-yellow, never white). land_column._how: A burning vehicle's own black column on land (the ruling, section 3: black, the lit side 40 to 60 and the shade 15 to 30, 3 m wide at the hull, 10 to 12 m at 30 m up, 25 to 35 m at 100 m, rising 150 to 250 m and bending downwind, pale only above 100 m). Measured on the wreck shot from 700 m: 10.5 m wide at 33 m up, 34 m at 100 m, its top near 190 m. Without from_m here: a tank's fire has no column of its own, as before.
land_column._mends: The art director 06:43Z 22 November: the column's top from 700 m ended in a rounded sausage tip, its puffs twisted like a rope. Its puffs now live 34 to 44 s, climb at 24 to 40 m/s, drift 0.7 to 1.5 of the wind and grow to 9 to 15 of the fire's width, from a wider head, rougher; and they pale a little and thin away as they climb, by pale_up_m 180, pale_up_pow 2.5 and thin_up 0.95 (see oil_fires.ablaze), so the top goes to nothing over its last 40 to 60 m and leans with the wind. 216 pieces at 2 minutes, against 243 before.

late._how: A long fire burning down (the ruling, section 3: 'in a long battle, after 3 to 5 minutes the flames drop to 1 to 2 m and the smoke goes grey-brown and thinner'). Each fire picks its own moment between from_s seconds after it was lit (by its seed, so a field of wrecks lit together never burn down together) and over by_s seconds, smoothly, its flames go to flames of their height and width (a tank's 3 m deck fire to about 1 to 1.5 m over the deck), its lamp and ground glow to light of their strength, its soot and its own smoke toward column_colour, and its land column's new puffs toward column_colour at their foot and column_top above, at column_alpha of their ink. Puffs already laid keep their colour, so the column greys from the bottom up. Without by_s: never, as before.

join._how: A knocked-out tank burns as one fire (the frame study of 22 November: the ground scene lit a wreck as six to eight fires of its own along the whole hull, one for each of the clip's fire and smoke beats, and they flickered and hopped as eight; the art director's ruling, section 3, wants one body of flame as wide as the engine deck). A fire lit within within_m of one already burning (on the level, and no more than up_m above or below it), neither of them over most_m across, joins it: that fire burns on as one, as long as the longer of them, growing smoothly over grow_s toward wide_m across at the most (each newcomer adds add of its own width; it never narrows), with one lamp, one glow and one column. The newcomer's number still finds it for BurnMove and BurnOut (its place kept as an offset; on a joined fire the first number that moves it moves it, the rest are not heard). No ground scene change is needed. Without within_m: every fire burns alone, as before.

lamp._how: A burning thing's lamp held steady (the frame study of 22 November: the lamps were handed out again every frame to the brightest of the moment, so a wreck's light hopped between its fires three or four times a second, and the ground and hull jumped with it). With ramp_s each fire, oil fire and jet keeps its lamp while it burns: ranked by its steady strength over its distance squared from the eye (keep times stronger if it held a lamp last frame, so two near alike do not swap), the first game.steady_lamps of them lit before any flash, the rest after. A fire's lamp comes up over ramp_s when lit and goes down over ramp_s when its flames end (and as it is put out), strength of the day's share times the square root of its width, flickering flicker by three smooth waves between flicker_hz, up of its width above it, reaching reach of its width and never under reach_least_m. Without ramp_s: as before.
lamp._mends: The art director 06:43Z 22 November: at dusk the deck and the turret's rear within 2 m should catch the lamp as they did before head C. land_strength 0.8 (0.3 in head C): the deck's lit strip from the battle camera at dusk 130 at the middle (86 in head C, 162 before it). The pre-check of 22 November: strength is read by every fire, so head C's 0.3 lit a ship's fire 1.6 times as strongly as before it, and 0.8 would have been 4.3 times. A ship's (strength) is 0.1875 again, as before head C (the old lamp's 0.25 times its mean flicker 0.75: one 8 m fire 12 m up, mean strength 0.133 by day before head C, 0.133 now); a fire on land's (land_strength, see fire.land_tongues) keeps 0.8. So too reach and up: a ship's lamp reaches 8 of its width from 0.6 of it up, as before head C; a fire on land's land_reach 3.3 and land_up 0.5, as in head C.

glow._how: A fire's warm light on the ground round it (the ruling, section 3: 'lights the ground within 5 to 8 m with a flicker'; the art director, 04:54Z 22 November: 'a warm ground glow with a soft fall-off and no hard rim, lighting the lower plates and near road wheels'). Soft warm pieces lying flat on the ground under the fire, a new one every every_s seconds living life_s and fading in over a third of it, so three overlap and their sum barely moves; r of the fire's width across, held between r_least_m and r_most_m; up_m over the ground; alpha (day_alpha of it by day), over its brightness past white; all of one fire flicker together by flicker between flicker_hz. Only for a fire within above_m of the ground (a ship's deck fire high over the sea lights no sea), and less as it is put out. Without every_s: none, as before.

shake._how: A short jolt on hits inside sizes.<kind>.shake_within_m, scaled by size and nearness: strength = scale * (1 - distance / within)^2. Hits beyond the radius never shake it. A setting turns shake off.

push_m._note: big bombs add a slight push away from the blast

shake.setting: Options: Camera shake on or off (default on)

movie.backlight: with a low sun behind the smoke, dust and cloud edges glow with a warm rim and the earth crown goes dark against it; keep the sun itself out of the camera's eye

depth.near: big, crisp, dark; debris passes the lens
depth.middle: the hit itself in full colour
depth.far: bursts small, softened and greyed by haze; flashes on the horizon; tall smoke columns standing over the far side of the field
depth.haze: battle_set's haze: starts 60 m, most at 700 m

movie.weight: big clouds climb slowly, debris on true gravity, dust settles for seconds; nothing pops in or out
movie.the_field_remembers: craters, scorch, smoke columns, burning wrecks and drifting haze build up over the battle

variety.turn: each version turned at random about the upright and leaned with the slope
variety._rule: a barrage's shells never land in step

muzzle._how: A gun firing. The flame is a ragged tongue along the bore with licks thrown sideways, under one frame; its lamp lights the gun and its pit, out before the next frame. Then grey-brown smoke rolls out, hangs and drifts. Big guns throw a ring of dust off the ground in front.

mg.smoke: a thin haze over the gun while it fires

tank_gun.case: ejected 0.7 s later (sound only within 40 m)

at_gun._note: fires flat from low down: the dust it throws off the ground in front can hide the gun for a moment, as it really did

mortar.smoke: a short puff up the tube's line

ship_aa._what: a ship's high-angle gun firing at aircraft (ShipGuns' heavy guns: the 5-inch, the 12.7 cm, the 4-inch and their like), from her deck over the sea: its flame and its own smoke along the bore, no dust ring (nothing under it but the sea 6 to 16 m below)

ship_main._what: a ship's big gun (a calibre of 200 mm or more) thrown low at a torpedo plane over the sea, as ship_aa but a battleship's flame and smoke

muzzle._naval: The sea's night fight, 25 November (look bible S7: 'gun flashes light the hulls'). A ship's own guns fired at ships, picked by the sea scene by calibre: naval_heavy 280 mm and up (the capital ships' main guns: 28 cm Scharnhorst to 46 cm Yamato), naval_medium 150 to 279 mm (the cruisers' 6-inch to 8-inch), naval_light under 150 mm (destroyers' 4- to 5.5-inch, and secondaries; a light cruiser with 127 to 140 mm main guns, Dido or Nagara, hulls 139 to 163 m, may take naval_medium for its reach). Fired by Muzzle as any row, one call a turret (or a gun: the lamp rule's merge sums and caps either way). Each lays a short flame at the muzzle (flame_m), a fireball ahead of it (fireball_m long, fireball_wide of that across, burning fireball_s, fireball_core at its root, fireball_colour through and fireball_edge at its rim, the lobes nearest the muzzle held at the root's near-white for fireball_hold_s: the secondary flash, the propellant's fuel-rich gas burning again in the air, Klingenberg and Heimerl, Gun Muzzle Blast and Flash, 1992; the lengths [EST] from period photographs of 16-inch broadsides, about two barrel lengths, and scaled down by the cube root of the charge, about 300 kg for a 16-inch, 15 to 40 kg for a 6- to 8-inch, 7 kg for a 5-inch, NavWeaps' gun pages; a measured 152 mm howitzer's secondary flash, about 8 m long at 27 ms and gone in about 100 ms, Steward, AFIT 2011, scales by the cube root to about 25 m and 0.3 s for a 16-inch, 9 to 10 m for a 6-inch and 7 m and 85 ms for a 5-inch), a smoke ring on the big guns (ring_m grown, rolling ring_ahead_m down the line of fire over ring_s, ring_puffs puffs each grown to ring_grow of the ring's radius, so it reads as one soft ring and not beads), and its own brown-grey cloud (cloud_m, smoke_colour, smoke_s; no billows, no dust ring: nothing under it but the sea). Its lamp (lamp_cd candelas at night at full, whatever game.lamp_candela_at_full is, coloured lamp_colour) reaches lamp_reach_m, about a hull's length for the band (a destroyer 115 m: Fletcher 114.8, Fubuki 118.4; a cruiser 190 m: Brooklyn 185.4, Baltimore 205.3, Leander 169; a battleship 240 m: King George V 227, Scharnhorst 235, Bismarck 251, Iowa 270), and goes down over lamp_s. It hangs lamp_out_m out along the bore's level way and lamp_up_m up from the fireball's middle, about half her length out and a quarter of it up (the look reviews of 25 November: a lamp by the fireball, a few metres off her side, burnt a spot of 40 to 110 lux on the plating by the gun and left her ends 6 to 8 stops darker; hung two fifths of her length up it lit her from overhead, as a star shell does, the light 48 to 54 degrees up and her deck as bright as her side; hung as now the light comes to her side 29 to 32 degrees up, over the water, her deck takes under half what her side does, and her side is lit end to end within about 1.4 stops). lamp_cd is half the reach squared. After a broadside at night, merged into one lamp of twice a turret's, her side plating gets about 1.9 to 2.3 lux by the gun and 0.8 at her ends, a little over what the land's passed lamp gives the ground at its foot (1.5 lux; 4.7 was overlit), and the water under the lamp about 9.2 to 9.4 lux, under the 9.9 lux that on this darker sea paint sends the eye what the land's overlit 4.7 did [EST, a look choice: a real 16-inch fireball, some 900 square metres at 1,700 to 1,900 K, is of the order of 10^7 to 10^8 cd, which would white the night out; to set the level on the Mac scale the three lamp_cd together, after step 11's night key and with the night lane's searchlight share, as effects-lamps-for-sea.md says]. By day (day_lamp, at game.day_lamp_share) every naval row lights its hull, a lift of about 0.5 lux on a side under the sea's 7-lux sun, as howitzer and ship_main do: game._day's small guns (under 75 mm, machine guns, rifles) light nothing by day, and a 100 to 140 mm gun is bigger than the 105 mm howitzer. Sound is not the kit's: sound/mix/mix.json.

naval_heavy._what: a capital ship's main gun, 280 mm and up (Muzzle, one call a turret)

naval_medium._what: a cruiser's main gun, 150 to 279 mm (Muzzle, one call a turret)

naval_light._what: a destroyer's gun, or a big ship's secondary, under 150 mm (Muzzle, one call a mount)

muzzle._day_lamp: By day only rows with day_lamp light the ground (at game.day_lamp_share); tank guns, anti-tank guns, machine guns, rifles and mortars do not (art director 21:16Z).

veil._how: Art director 06:19Z, the desert: a tank or field gun's shot (any row with dust_ring_m; a towed gun's muzzle socket too) raises the ground round the muzzle in a veil spread along the line of fire, rising a metre or two (every other puff a low dense skirt on the ground, dust.vehicles.low_skirt), that hides the gun and its line of sight for hide_s, then thins to haze_alpha and lingers on the wind. by_ground: where it rises (and how thick); the ring itself takes the ground's own paint and grounds.<g>.dust against earth's.
veil._lumps: Art director 18:28Z: the desert veil gets the tank gun's treatment (muzzle.billows), lumps and never upright sheets. lumps: that many times puffs, each a lump lump_r of a sheet's radius across (so several sizes, 0.7 to 2 m for a tank gun) and lump_thick of the veil's thickness (thick ones and thin ones, with gaps), with the billows' firm heart and rough outline, lit as one cloud; every other one a mound lying on the ground, the rest thrown up lump_up_m over it and thinner the higher by lump_pale_up. lump_tuft_share of them thin to haze_alpha by hide_s and linger for life_s as the veil did; the others are gone soon after hide_s. With game.near_eye_fade_m it fades out near the camera. Tried at twice the count and size: a pale wash over the lower frame. 0 or no key: the ten upright sheets as before.

billows._how: Art director 17:52Z on build 1746's test, where a tank gun fired 4 m from two riflemen and its smoke lay over them as one even beige gauze: a heavy gun blinding the men beside it is right, but it must read as dust, not fog. A field gun's shot (a row whose flame_m is 0.5 or more) raises a cloud in three layers, each a scatter of lumps of several sizes and thicknesses with gaps between, never one sheet. low: dense mounds of the ground's own dust resting on the ground under and ahead of the muzzle, over reach of its dust ring (shares of dust_ring_m, behind to ahead) and wide of it to each side, each low_r of the ring across. mid: lumps of dust and smoke (smoke_mix of game.muzzle_smoke) thrown up over them, mid_up_m above the ground, mid_r of the ring across, thinner by pale_up and sooner gone the higher they start. top: the gun's own smoke thrown along the bore from the muzzle and scattered off it at scatter_mps, top_r of the flame's length across (plus 0.2 m); the further it flies and the higher, the thinner. So the cloud is heaviest low and near the muzzle and thins upward, and men behind it come clear from the head down. Each layer is thick for a little under half its life, then thins: mid and low live clear_s, top top_s, so the thick part is gone in 1.5 to 2 s. Of the low mounds, tuft_share settle to haze_alpha by haze_by_s and drift on the wind for tuft_s as tufts. low, mid, top are a tank gun's counts (a wider ring and a longer flame throw more); dust goes by the ground's own (grounds.<g>.dust against earth's). heart, inner: how solid a lump is and how far out (a firm body with a short soft edge shows its lumpy outline, rough); shade: its sunward side lit and far side shadowed. A lump never sinks into the ground: its middle stays its own radius clear of it. Without low, a gun smokes as it did before (17 soft puffs along the bore). The gun's low dust ring (dust_ring_m) and the desert's veil (veil, sand only) are as they were.

dry._how: Art director 06:08Z 20 November on build 1758's west still on sand: half a second after the shot the dry lumps and the gun's smoke wisps were still one soft cloud, and two riflemen 4 m off the line of fire, seen across it, almost vanished. On a ground named in by_ground (its number: how many times the pieces) a heavy gun's blast (a row with dust_ring_m) raises four to six big dense lumps and nothing thin. tall of them stand where the blast strikes the ground hardest, at the muzzle's two flanks and just ahead of it, never behind it: each tall_r of the ring across with two shoulders, about man-high for a tank gun. low of them are heaps of two lobes farther down the line of fire, one to a stretch with clear ground between, each low_r of the ring across, smaller the farther out. The gun's own smoke is puffs dense puffs at the muzzle, puff_r of the flame across, taking smoke_as_dust of the dust's colour. Every piece is alpha thick to inner of its radius with a lumpy outline (rough) and is lit as a thing with form (light: how strongly its sunward side is lit and its far side shadowed): in the preview its lit top lands 1.08 to 1.10 times the ground, its shadow side about two thirds. The heaps are gone by clear_s; the tall ones hold to near_s, thinning, the cloud that gives the gun away. Colour: the ground under the muzzle as the game's screen shows it (FBattleEffects::GroundColour), shade times lighter times as light at its middle, written to land on it by picture.to_land; where the game cannot say, the ground row's dust paint. The ring, the billows and the veil are not drawn there. Neither tall nor lumps (build 1758's lumps: lumps, lump_r, belly, crown_r, crown_up, wide, reach, smoke): all as before.
dry._low: Art director 08:03Z 20 November on build 1762's still from 60 m, a fifth of a second after the shot: the young lumps read as small pale balls. With low_s the dust is born low: until low_s.0 seconds old each lump and heap lies along the ground low_flat times as high as it is wide (as wide again as keeps its bulk), the way blast dust first skirts out, in its plain middle tone with no lit top and no shadow side, its dense part reaching only low_soft of the way out it will, so the young skirt has a soft edge. By low_s.1 seconds it has risen round, firmed and earned its light, so half a second after the shot it is the lump the art director passed in build 1762. The gun's smoke puffs, off the ground, keep their round shape and only firm and come into their light as late. shade is now six parts in a hundred either side of its middle, so each lump is of its own shade. No low_s: born round and lit, as in build 1762. Build 1764's stills from 60 m (09:28Z 20 November): the young skirt, soft-edged and in one flat tone a little under the ground's, was lost on the game's rippled sand, so nothing marked the shot for a third of a second. low_lit is the share of its light and shade a mound is born with: at 0.5 its top sits at about the ground's own tone (never the pale of a lit lump) and its foot is darker, so it reads as a low heap of dust; low_soft 1 gives it its firm edge from birth. No low_lit: 0, as in build 1764.

hot._how: Art director 07:08Z: close to the eye (within_m) a ground gun's flash, a machine gun's (Shots, mg) or a field gun's (Muzzle), is lit from within as the air guns' close flash: a yellow-white root at the muzzle (root to root_edge, its rim hot), an orange body (orange, its rim rim) with dense rims, shrinking rather than going see-through. Past within_m as before. Art director 13:54Z on the game's own frames (build 1720), where that read as a sticker: with tongues here, the close flash is instead a small white-yellow root right at the muzzle (root), melting into yellow, then the orange body, widest a third of the way out, which breaks into 3 to 5 ragged tongues with red only at their ends (red), and 2 to 4 short licks thrown sideways; its length is rolled between long x its usual length every round (mg_flame_m for a machine gun, 1.4 x flame_m for a gun), so no two match. Dense inside, its edge a pixel or two soft. glow: a thin glow glow_m past the flame, that opaque at dusk and glow_day_share of it by day. over: how far past white the root burns (see picture.lit_gain). wide: half its width, as a share of its usual length. Art director 16:30Z on build 1732's stills (root cream at 235,231,216, orange 230,152,4 with no blue: candy): these colours are WRITTEN values, aimed through the game's curve (picture._how). root at over 4 lands 253,250,234, luma 249, over a spot 5 to 9 px across on a 1600 still. orange lands about 234,141,41 (her 235,140,40; written 235,140,40 it landed 234,150,0). yellow_over: how far past white the yellow burns (1.175, as it did when over was 1.5; absent, a share of over). halo: a soft card of the root's colour round the root, that opaque at its inner edge and nothing halo_m further out, in place of the game's bloom (never over 0.25; 0 or absent: none). At 0.08 and 0.028 m it lifts the picture a quarter of the way to the root at most, 3 to 4.5 px out on a 1600 still. Art director 18:05Z on build 1746's stills (root 252,249,233, white for about 5 px along the bore, the glow down to the ground by about 8 px on a 1600 still): the game's own bloom already gives the glow, so the card is dropped (halo 0; halo_m kept for the day it is wanted again).

ground_cases._how: The grit up close (art director): within within_m of the eye, a ground machine gun (Shots with weapon mg) drops its spent brass out of the bottom of its receiver every round (as the war's machine guns did), falling with a little scatter to build a small heap under and beside the gun where the gunner lies; a towed or field gun (Muzzle at_gun, howitzer) opens its breech after_s after each shot and throws its big brass case out behind, where it lies for minutes, so the cases pile up behind the gun through a fight. A tank's cases stay inside it. Each case is a brass tube lit as metal (art director 07:08Z): a bright band toward the sun with a glint (glint, shine), a shade side and underside (shade), the dark open mouth (mouth) at one end when it is turned to the eye, and a soft contact shadow on the ground once it lies there (contact_shadow). Past most_lying cases lying at once, a new one lies only a moment. Each gun's cases use their own dice, so its rounds, strikes and smoke fall as they always did; a recipe without ground_cases draws none. They are left out when the screen is past three fifths full.

mg._note: art director 07:08Z: out of the bottom of the receiver (the MG 34 and 42, the Bren, the DP, the Browning, the Vickers), rifle-calibre cases about 6 cm; they lie long enough to heap up

bullet_strike._how: Art director 21:16Z: small dust spurts where a burst's rounds strike the ground (Shots, given the ground). About three rounds in ten kick one (pre-check 21:34Z: at one in two a firing gun cost about 16 puffs): a quick upward spurt and a low puff in the ground's dust colour, gone in under a second, scattered about the aim point by spread_mil of the range.

bullet_ricochet._how: Effects (R2), small arms off armour (Brian, 25 November 15:58Z: 'are bullets taking out german tanks? cannon fire or bazookas should be the only thing taking them out ... bullets should be bouncing off it'; off unless -TheaterLandRicochet (release 2, on trial)). ShotsOnArmour: a rifle's or machine gun's burst striking a tank, an assault gun, a self-propelled gun, an armoured car or a half-track (LandPlay::ArmouredVehicle) bounces off her plate, as the war film's machine gun raking a tank. Each round that strikes, spread over the plate about the aim (bullet_strike.spread_mil of the range, held to spread_m across and up it) and inside the room the battle says the plate has there, edge_m short of its edges (none in the air past her edge, on a curve that leaves the plate, or inside her), where her plate is when it strikes (riding with her as she moves: its flash, sparks and paint carried with her): a two-frame (flash_s) near-white flash flash_m across, burning flash_over past white, in a faint warm halo (halo_m, halo_alpha), each held to flash_least_px on the screen (so by day at 150 to 600 m each strike still twinkles white); sparks a round thrown in a cone_deg cone about the mirror of its way in, opened square_open_deg more the squarer it struck and never nearer the plate than least_off_deg, at spark_mps skewed by the power spark_uneven (most slow and short, a few fast and long), spark_wide_m wide, burning spark_over past white, falling, white-yellow (spark) cooling to orange (spark_old) by the end of its life, gone in spark_life_s (under 0.3 s), going out before it falls back onto a roof or a glacis, onto her own floor under the plate (her deck under her turret, her track guard under her hull's side: the battle's) or into the ground; chip_chance of rounds a faint grey puff of paint (chip, chip_alpha). A tracer that strikes (the gun's own one in tracer.one_in) is drawn to the plate and never past it, and while it still burns (tracer.life_s) tracer_chance of them go off again as a ricochet: tracer.ricochet.deflect_deg off the plate the way it was going, up to tracer_yaw_deg aside, at tracer.ricochet.slower of the tracer's speed, falling (tracer_drop), for tracer_life_s, its way kinked kink_deg at kinks moments as it tumbles and kink_slow slower at each, tracer_alpha bright (dimmer than the tracer coming in, so a far tank is not hidden behind them) and dimming; its streak tracer_streak_s of its flight (0.014 s: 4 to 6 m, shorter than a tank at 600 m and about half a hull at 150 m); a way headed down turned up as shallowly (as a skip off the ground would), and drawn only to where it meets the ground. Never a dust spurt on the armour. Far off: where a metre on the plate is under full_px on the screen, that share of sparks (never under far_least of them, never under one a round), each the root of it bigger and drawn out to spark_long_px long (never a bead), holding its full strength spark_hold_far of its life and cooling only spark_cool_far of the way to spark_old (so none fades to a dull brown fleck over her paint); a busy screen (the room over halve_past full) half as many, a quarter past four fifths full. Every key is read with its default.

struck._how: Effects (R2), the blood mist at a bullet's strike (Brian, 26 November: "i do want a better look when a guy gets hit", "like a puff or mist of blood"; the scene's -TheaterLandHitMist, Battle::Struck). The look is what a rifle's or a machine gun's round truly did, sober: on the side it enters almost nothing, a small pale puff of cloth dust off the tunic or webbing (entry), gone in a quarter second; on the side it leaves, where it passed through (through: the odds by the round, a limb's times limb_k, the head's head_k), a fine dull red-pink mist thrown on along its path a forearm to an arm long (mist: pieces strung along it by speed_mps against drag, so 0.3 to 0.8 m), widening (r1_m) and thinning, most of it gone by 0.3 to 0.5 s, and a few heavier dark drops falling short within a metre (drops); a head strike a shorter, denser puff (head). No fountain, no pool, no spurt, nothing that hangs, no lamp, no mark on the ground: ten pieces at the most, all gone within the second. Far off each mist piece is held at least_px across and thinned to match (never under least_keep of itself), so at 100 m it is a few pixels of dark pink and at 300 m next to nothing; nothing at all past within_m, or with the screen's room past room_share full. Colours written to land on the game's curve (game_curve.py write; the land battle's grade has its own under land_grade.men.struck): the mist lands 110,66,46 young (green well over blue, so it holds red-brown, not mauve, as it blends into a blue-grey sky) and darker and browner as it thins, 92,66,54 (never paler: pale reads as dust), its alpha carrying the thinning (hold 0.06: it starts to thin early); its pieces start a little apart along the path (exit_step_m) and across it (side_m, by each piece's own jitter), sized by their place along it (r1_share_k) and the first thinner (first_alpha_k), so seen end-on it is an uneven smear, not a ball (no row: as before), the drops 58,26,25, the cloth 152,144,128. The red is the art director's to rule on. Remove on (or the whole row) and nothing is drawn.

through._how: The chance the round passes through and leaves the far side. A rifle's and a machine gun's full-power rounds (7.92 mm, .303, .30-06, 7.62 mm at 750 to 850 m/s) at battle ranges mostly went through the body and almost always through a limb; a sub-machine gun's and a pistol's slower 9 mm or .45 mostly stayed in the body. Times limb_k through an arm or a leg (at most 1), head_k through the head.

tracer._how: Brian 2026-11-18: 'i want tracer fire shown as well. 1 out of every 5 bullets with yellow'. As a belt was loaded: every fifth round of a gun is a tracer; the four between are not seen. Out of step between guns.
tracer._most: Art director 01:31Z: a near streak stays thin, no brighter than a far one, and is long on the screen for a frame or two (a whip, not a beam). A tracer is laid along its true heading, as wide on the screen from end to end, and no wider than most_px in the middle of the screen (times day_width by day: 7.5 px; a far one is 4.5; up to a sixth wider toward the edges, as the picture draws everything there). 0 takes the limit off. Passing a few metres off it drew 20 px and more before.

ricochet._note: a tracer striking the ground or armour sometimes skips up at an angle: a real sight in films and footage

picture._how: The game's picture (CampaignCameraPawn.cpp: Unreal's film curve, saturation 1.07, contrast 1.08, warm highlights, film toe 0.6) holds plain white (255) down to about 226, darkens and warms the darks (grey 60 shows as 31) and takes the blue out of a strong orange. tools/battle-fx/game_curve.py is that road in numbers: `lands` says what a written colour shows as in the game, `write` what to write to land on a number. lit_gain: the game's material multiplies every colour by this (the wrapper sets M_Highlight's Brightness to it) and the kit writes every colour that much darker, so all looks as before; but the hottest lights (muzzle.hot.over, tracer.day_over) are written up to that much past white. 1 or absent: nothing changes. Art director 16:30Z (build 1732): the game-wide curve and bloom stay as they are, and a flash's root burns near white by the kit's own gain; 4 times white lands a warm white at 253,250,236, where 1.5 landed cream at 238,234,222. Colours are written in 8 bits of linear light, so at 4 the darkest paints keep fewer steps: dark smoke and clods through the game's curve moved by 2 to 5 levels at most 12 (checked on a howitzer burst, a burning fall and an oil fire).
picture._to_land: What to write, 0 to 255, for the game's screen to show a grey of 0, 15, 30 and so on to 255: the game's film curve and grade turned round (python3 tools/battle-fx/game_curve.py table; make it again if the grade in CampaignCameraPawn.cpp changes). The kit reads a colour off it channel by channel, between the steps, where it must match something the screen already shows: a gun's dust on dry ground against the ground under it (muzzle.dry). Earth colours land within about 3 of the colour asked.

air_guns._how: Brian 2026-11-18 19:35Z: 'make the gun fire very realistic and the tracer fire too'. Guns on aircraft (AirGun, called every frame while a trigger is down). The battle sends where each gun is, the point it is laid on (lead and convergence are the battle's), and the aircraft's own velocity; the kit lays each round from where the muzzle was at that moment. A round flies at muzzle_mps plus the aircraft's speed, slows (drag, a share of its speed lost a second) and falls (drop). Every round flickers at the muzzle; one in tracer_every is the ruled tracer (tracer.colour, tracer.streak_m), burning for tracer_s. The sound director's air.gunsByCalibre uses the same three families: rifle, heavy, 20 mm cannon.

aa25._what: a ship's 20 to 25 mm guns (the Oerlikon, the Japanese 25 mm, the German 2 cm, the Italian Breda 20 mm): ShipGuns' light guns of kind aa25, laid by eye along their tracers from her decks (Brian, 21 November 18:06Z: ships fire back at the planes attacking them). The 20 mm cannon's row, a tracer in three (the gunners hosed by the tracer), each burning longer, as a ship's gun reaches out to 1.5 to 2 km
aa25._fx_air_r2: fx-air r2 (art director, Midway 06b and Samar b34a 02): a ship's light AA is a hose of tracer, not a ladder of dashes, and burns out at its reach. hose: each round lays a thin line back to the round fired before it, drawn where both are now (hose its opacity, hose_px its width in the pixels the scene tells the kit, hose_mix how far its colour goes from the glow's to the core's, hose_s the least seconds between its points: a 25 mm's hose runs through every second round), so a burst is one line through its rounds, curving as the gun swings and the rounds slow and drop; a new burst starts a new hose. ship_hue: the nation's ship colours (air_guns.tracers.nations.<n>.ship) where it has them. burn_out_m: a tracer burns until it has flown that far (the art director's 2 km for a 20 mm, 3.5 km for a 40 mm), dwindling from dwindle_from_m to dwindle_to of its strength and dwindle_wide of its width; tail_fade and core_tail_fade: its glow's and core's tail end that much fainter than the head, so each reads as a moving streak; its core keeps its own colour near the eye. drag 0.22 (0.16 for aa40) from the scenes' 0.38 and 0.3: the gunners lay their lead for an average of 0.8 of the muzzle speed (ShipGuns' Tof), which these give out to about 2 km, and the rounds reach their burn-out. Without these keys the row is as the scenes carry it.

aa40._what: a ship's 37 to 40 mm guns (the Bofors, the 1.1-inch, the British pom-pom, the German 3.7 cm, the Soviet 37 and 45 mm): ShipGuns' light guns of kind aa40, a slow heavy beat of big red-orange tracers, every round a tracer (their clips were loaded so), each burning out to about 3 km, with a heavy flash and a puff of smoke at every round

close._how: The close view: only within licks_within_m of the eye does a row's flicker throw close_licks short side licks raked aft, with a lamp of close_lamp (night only, as every small gun's); only within cases_within_m does every round drop its spent case (case_m long, case_d_m across, case_colour, case_dark on its far face) and belt link (link_m, link_colour) from a chute chute_back_m behind the muzzle and chute_down_m under it, kicked out at throw_mps, torn aft by the air (drag) and falling at case_sink_mps or link_sink_mps, tumbling tumble radians a second and glinting (glint), gone in life_s. Left out first when the room fills.
close._art_director_0440: Art director 04:40Z item 6: close view only: cases and links from the wing gun chutes and from the turrets that dumped them overboard, drawn within 60 m. Heavy machine gun licks 0 to 2, with the small lamp, for guns within 30 m.

air_guns._numbers: Rates and speeds are the middle of each family: rifle calibre 900-1,200 a minute at 745-905 m/s; 12.7-13 mm 750-950 at 750-890; 20 mm 520-750 at 600-880. The battle can pass a gun's own rate and speed. drag is set so a round keeps the speed it really kept downrange: a .50 about 700 m/s at 500 m and 530 at 1,000 m (0.36), a rifle round about 520 at 450 m (0.5). tracer_s is how long the tracer burns: the .50's to about 1,450 m, the rifle round's and the 20 mm's to about 900 to 1,100 m. Each gun runs a few per cent fast or slow, so wing guns drift out of step as real ones did.
air_guns._flash_hot: Art director 06:19Z: the flash lit from within, as the fireball: a white-yellow root at the muzzle (luma 235 or more over its first quarter), a saturated orange body (flash_orange) going to a deeper orange at its edges (flash_rim) so a rim over the sky never turns peach, and a fading tip, all emissive, no dark crease. Dense to its edge; its second frame is about half by shrinking, never by going see-through. The heavy machine gun's close view (flicker and licks) always; the cannon's whole flash where its row sets hot_flash; the cannon's is the bigger, hotter one (twice the heavy machine gun's length).
air_guns._flash: Art director 21:07Z, cannon (rows with licks): a hot pale heart at the muzzle (flash_heart) with orange only toward its edges; a ragged forward tongue two to three times the side licks' length; short side licks raked aft by the airstream; uneven, never the same twice; one frame at full, a second at about half. The machine guns' flicker passed as it is.
air_guns._flash_least_px: Art director 04:40Z: from the strategy camera a heavy machine gun's 0.45 m flash is half a pixel at 800 m; every muzzle flash (the flicker, or a cannon's hot heart) is held at least flash_least_px 2 px across on its flash frame and made fainter to match, from the kit's own shape, never a card: far off they read as twinkles. A row may set its own.

tracers._how: An air gun's tracer (art director 15:02Z 20 November, air-fates-look D, for Brian's 'more real istic chaser fire'; colours 15:38Z, G2). With this row every air tracer is alight life_s (a cannon's tracer_life_k of that), a streak streak_s seconds of its flight long (about 30 m for a .50; a row may set its own streak_s) that shortens as the round slows, a hot core in a glow no wider than two or three times the core, at its full strength until dim_from of its life, dimming to dim_to of it, then out over out_s, two or three frames. It flies in the world at the gun's speed plus the aircraft's own, slowing and dropping about 7 m, so a moving bomber's streams bend back like water from a hose. A cannon's (the row's cannon 1) is tracer_wide times as wide. nations: whose gun it is (AirGun's Nation), body the glow and core the hot middle, each written for the game's picture (game_curve.py write) with how far past white it burns; a nation's cannon colours where it has its own; default for no nation or one not listed. No more than most alight at once: as the count nears it the guns farthest from the eye go without first, those within always_within_m never. Without this row the tracers are the ruled yellow streak, as before.
tracers._white: The core burns white-hot (as far past white as the picture allows, picture.lit_gain) within white_within_m of the eye and its nation's own colour from white_beyond_m on: near white at close range, as ruled.
tracers._px: body_px and core_px are the glow's and the core's width by day in the pixels the scene tells the kit. The air scene draws 1072 across and tells the kit its window's 2881, so 9.6 and 3.2 are 5.3 and 1.8 px on a 1600 still (the art director's 3 px least stands, the glow three cores wide and soft). The ruled streak's 3.4 came out at 1.3 drawn pixels there, a hairline the Pearl Harbor film lost. A cannon's are tracer_wide times these. At dusk a streak is never under three quarters of these.
tracers._hose_most: fx-air r2: no more than hose_most ship guns' hose lines (a row's hose) at once; as the tracers' room passes 0.7 of most, the guns beyond always_within_m lose their hoses first, as their tracers.
tracers._glow_soft: Art director 19:52Z 20 November: solid across, the glow was a bar darker than a pale sky round a sky-pale core, a hollow tube, and end-on a ring. With glow_soft the glow is that strong beside the core and fades smoothly from the core's edge to nothing at its own, with no rim (by day; at dusk it is as it was), and the core stands at least 25 over the sky it crosses (us lands 255,236,212, red only in its glow). one_fan_px: a far gun's one-fan tracer is a solid dash that wide in the core's own colour, never an outlined oval.
tracers._one_fan: A gun farther than one_fan_beyond_m from the eye fires tracers of one piece (see one_fan_px): its core was a pixel wide there, and a tracer costs half as much. Without the key every tracer is glow and core.
