air._how: An air scene (its own FBattleEffects, UseAirDistance): its strategy camera stands 800 to 2,000 m off the fight (feel-benchmark gap 3), so it draws puffs out to draw_beyond_m, not game.draw_beyond_m's 1,500 m.

air_hit._how: Rounds striking an aircraft (AirHit, at the point hit, carried with that aircraft): a hot spit on the skin with two or three short tongues, sparks thrown off and slowed by the air so they fall away behind, a scrap or two of skin tumbling off (some bare metal catching the light), and a small dark puff left hanging where the hit was. All scale with the hitting gun's air_guns.<kind>.strike_m, so 20 mm hits are about twice a .50's. No ball of fire: a hit that sets fuel alight is the battle's call (a fire trail).
air_hit._art_director_0440: Art director 04:40Z: a hit's puff hangs 3 to 4 s (smoke_s), growing to smoke_r1 times the strike size; from the strategy camera the spit on the skin is never under least_px 2 px on its flash frame, so far off a hit reads as a twinkle.

sparkle._how: A rifle-calibre or heavy machine gun round striking an aircraft (art director 15:02Z 20 November, air-fates-look D): a bright sparkle of one or two frames and nothing more, no puff and no scraps. points of them within within_s, the first where the round struck and the rest scatter_m about it on the skin, each size_m across for a .50 (by the gun's strike_m), alight life_s, burning over times past white, never under least_px on the screen (the pixels the scene tells the kit). With this row; without it a hit is as it was.

burst._how: A 20 mm shell striking an aircraft (the same ruling; a row of air_guns with cannon 1): the small flash as before, sparks of them, fragments scraps of skin, and one black-grey puff puff_m across hanging puff_s where the hit was, a ragged roundish ball of a main puff and puff_lobes smaller ones crowding it (art director 19:52Z: one rough puff read as a bird or a moth). With this row; without it a cannon's hit is as it was.

spurt._how: The owner's item 2 (26 November: 'i like the debris coming off the planes when hit', 'oil streaking across a hit plane's windscreen'): the spray that leaves a hole in the moments after the strike, before any trail starts (AirHit's Part, the battle's Hit Fx Part: fuel, oil or coolant; skin and anything else none). OFF until on is 1: the overlay battle-fx-air-spurt.json the air scene lays with its word turns it on. Each puff leaves the hole where the hole is at its moment, with the aircraft's speed, and drag takes that off it so it falls back past the tail. puffs (how many), over_s (the seconds they are laid over), life_s, r0_m and r1_m (radius at birth and at the end), alpha, stretch (drawn out along the flight), drag (a second), kick_mps (off the skin), rough. Colours from the trail row the battle draws for the same thing afterwards (fuel air_trails.mist, oil air_trails.oil, coolant air_trails.glycol), with their shadow; oil pulled tint_share of the way to tint (engine oil is dark brown, the oil trail's smoke grey). most_a_frame: sprays begun at one moment, at most. least_px, least_keep: from far off a puff is held to least_px across and keeps least_keep of its opacity there, so it blinks and fades, never pops. Its own dice (the place, the moment, the part), never the kit's shared ones.

air_trails._how: A trail from a moving point on an aircraft (TrailStart, TrailMove every frame, TrailStop). Puffs are laid every spacing_m along the path, each drawn smear x spacing longer behind it so they join in one line, and left hanging in the air (carried: the share of the aircraft's speed they keep) to drift with the wind. Each frame the young end is drawn from the point back to the newest puff, so a trail starts at the engine. A trail comes to full over ramp_s, darkening from colour to colour_full over darken_s; each puff widens from r0_m to r1_m as it hangs for life_s (grow: below 1 widens early, above 1 late) and pales toward colour_old. lumpy (0 to 1) makes some puffs bigger lumps and the rest smaller and shorter lived, and the smear shrinks over smear_s, so an old trail breaks into uneven lumps; rise_mps lifts the smoke. Fire adds ragged tongues streaming back about flame_m from the root, and its smoke starts at the flame's tips.

smoke._what: a damaged engine: thin and dark at the engine, widening (about three times by 2 s) and breaking into paler lumps

fire._what: an engine or tank on fire: ragged flame streaming aft from the root, black smoke rising from its tips

glycol._what: a holed radiator: a thin white vapour that soon thins out

air_trails._art_director: 21:27Z: 20 mm hits, glycol and the fire trail at distance PASS. Engine fire: ragged tongues tearing free of the cowl and streaming aft past the wing root, a pale yellow heart at the cowl and deep orange along the tongues, a new length and shape every frame, black smoke rising from the flame tips. Smoke: thin and dark at the engine, about three times wider by 2 s and still widening, breaking into uneven lumps, paler and thinner with age, each lump hanging where it was laid. 21:37Z: the smoke trail, the 10 s fire trail and the glycol start PASS. The fire's tongues stand off the skin as they stream aft (flame_lift_m, above or below), so a few break the outline; the heart hugs the cowl.
air_trails._load: Pre-check 21:34Z: puffs a trail are about life_s x speed / spacing_m (the lumpy rows lose about an eighth to their short-lived small puffs). At 120 m/s: smoke about 80, fire about 105, glycol about 35. The room is game.max_puffs, shared by everything; when it is short the farthest puffs go first, so a far trail loses length first.
air_trails._art_director_0440: Art director 04:40Z (Brian's air clip, feel-benchmark gap 3): smoke hangs, a sky full of hanging trails is the picture. A fire trail lives 30 s and a straggler's smoke 20 s; to fit the 3,000-puff room, past thin_after_s (the old life) only one puff in thin_keep_one_in hangs on, growing on as it did and thinning slowly, so an old trail is fewer, bigger lumps. A burning plane's flame is half its span (TrailStart's span; flame_of_span), at most flame_most_m 10 m, ragged and flickering, streaming back from the root, black smoke from its tips; from the strategy camera its heart is never under flame_least_px 4 px. Gun smoke stays short.
air_trails._art_director_0459: Art director 04:59Z on 299e504: the trails faded too pale too soon. Each kept puff (one in thin_keep_one_in) now thickens to thin_alpha times its opacity by thin_after_s as the three beside it go, so the young trail looks as it did; it hangs the whole of life_s (a small one going early left a gap), holds full to thin_hold of its life, and is drawn out along the path over the gap to the next one kept, so the old trail is one dark line of lumps that touch. Measured at 2.5 km off the beam (sky 212): fire head 61, first third 103, second third 110, old 109, oldest 105; straggler smoke head 131, first third 143, second third 147. Fire: by day a tongue off the skin must read as fire against the sky, so flame_alpha [at the cowl, at the tip] and flame_hold keep it opaque, flame_wide widens it, and it stands off the skin by flame_lift_of_length, licking out above and below the fuselage; tip_smoke lays black smoke right at each tongue's tip (that opacity, living tip_smoke_s, widening to tip_smoke_r_of_flame of the flame's length), above or below as the tongue is, so there is no gap between flame and smoke. Old recipes without these keys draw as before.
air_trails._art_director_0525: Art director 05:25Z on 1295edc: trails PASS. Kept evenly the old trail read as a string of beads, so thin_ragged tears it: the gap to the next puff kept is thin_keep_one_in times 1 plus or minus thin_ragged, and the puff's size by up to half of it (fire at 2.5 km: 66 | 102 | 109 | 107 | 107). A tongue is fixed at its root and free at its tip: flame_lift_curve is the power of the way along it by which its stand-off comes, so it is rooted on the skin at the fire with the yellow-white heart there and only its tip licks out above or below, sweeping back, going orange to flame_tip_colour (dark red) into the black smoke laid at its tip.
air_trails._art_director_1413: Art director 14:13Z on build 1722's air frames: the falling planes' trails read as beads on a string, the spacing seeming to depend on speed. Each puff was a lens drawn out behind it, so two neighbours met only at their thin faint tips, and past thin_after_s most were gone. With ribbon 1 a trail is one strip: each piece runs from its own point back to the piece laid before it, wherever that has drifted to, as wide and as dark at that edge as that piece is now, so the two share the edge with no overlap and no gap at any speed; the strip leaves each edge along the way the aircraft flew there, so it bends through a turn or a spin. core: the share of its half width that is dense, thinning to nothing at its sides. drift: how much of the sideways scatter it keeps; each piece takes most of the drift and rise of the one before it, so the strip meanders and never zig-zags, and its pieces all last as long, so it goes from its old end. One piece in thin_keep_one_in, and one wherever the path has turned keep_each_turn_deg, is also a long length that hangs the whole of life_s, growing thin_grow times wider; it comes into sight between join_from and join_by of thin_after_s as the short pieces go. From lumps_from of its life (a little sooner or later each, by thin_ragged) a length lets go of its neighbours, paling and narrowing to nothing at each end, then draws in to a soft lump: only the old end tears into lumps. Measured: room at 120 m/s, smoke 124 places (130 before) and fire 225 (225); close up on a 212 sky, fire 98 (101 before) and smoke 160 (158), with alpha raised a little (smoke 0.5 to 0.55, fire 0.9 to 0.96) since pieces no longer overlap. Recipes without ribbon draw as before.
air_trails._art_director_1522: Art director 15:22Z on 00c2860: level trails PASS; the two falls read as pen strokes, evenly black with ruled edges. A ribbon now ages over its first seconds: widen_by_s is the time by which a piece has widened from r0_m to r1_m (by the power grow: over 1 it stays thin at first, then spreads), and the lengths that hang on widen with it and then on to thin_grow times; it stays as black as it was laid until pale_from_s and pales to pale_to of its opacity by pale_by_s, short pieces and long lengths by the one clock; wide_wander makes its width wander along its length, each piece taking most of the last one's, so its edges swell and pinch in soft lumps, and a wide length's lumpy outline is gentler so it never combs into spikes. Measured on the fall preview 14 s into the fall (sky 208 to 211; the frame holds smoke about 2.5 to 7.5 s old, the burning plane itself is by then under the preview's ground): burning fall 3 px wide and 155 darker than the sky at its young end, 11 px and 130 darker at its old end (before: 2.4 to 5.7 px, 146 to 150 all along); spin 2.2 to 11 px, 134 to 87. Level flight from 2.5 km: fire 82 to 83 along its length, smoke 125 to 129. 16:01Z, falls PASS, and pale_to is split by kind: a burning plane's black smoke is one of the strongest grit cues, so fire keeps about 85% of its young darkness at its old end (pale_to 0.94; at 0.85 the level burning trail read mid-grey, 105), while a damaged engine's smoke goes grey (0.8). Darkness on the screen falls faster than opacity, so tune pale_to by measured luma. Recipes without widen_by_s, pale_to and wide_wander draw as 00c2860 did. It takes no more room.
air_trails._art_director_1708: Art director 17:08Z on build 1734's air frames: the old ends of the trails read as beads on a string, a dotted line and not smoke breaking up. From lumps_from of its life each long length let go of its neighbours and drew in to a lump; once the aircraft was gone, all that was left of its trail was in that stage at once, a row of even dark dashes about 50 m apart for 4 to 7 s. lumps_from 1 on smoke and fire: the strip stays whole to its end and thins to nothing over its last fifth (thin_hold, left as it was); a burning plane's keeps its darkness until that thinning. Only its last twentieth may still part, at a seventh of its darkness and less.
air_trails._engine_out: Art director 15:38Z 20 November (air-fates-look G1) for Brian's 'if a engine is out there should be a lot more dark smoke strains from that engine and directly behind it on the tail': a dead engine always smokes. tail_wide_m: how wide the smoke is as it passes the tail, tail_m behind its source; the aircraft's own wake spreads it that fast, and the row's r1_m and widen_by_s widen it on after. fire: 1.5 m at the nacelle, 5 to 6 m past the tail, the densest black. oil (out and windmilling): 1.2 to 1.5 m and 4 to 5 m, dark grey, 0.6 to 0.7 opaque at the nacelle, lumpy, one torn column, a gout gout_wide times as wide and gout_alpha times as dense for gout_s every gout_every_s as the oil spits; wisps: the share of its pieces that throw a shred off its edge. streak (the fire put out, the airscrew feathered): 0.8 to 1 m and about 3 m, 0.3 to 0.4 opaque at the nacelle paling to 0.15 by 60 m behind; it never clears while the caller keeps it. doused: the extinguisher's white-grey puff for for_s, the flames of a burning trail shrinking back to the nacelle over flame_shrink_s, then the streak on its own (then_streak), grey at first and darkening. glycol: thinning to fade_to of itself over fade_over_s, then the streak. A change of kind is TrailStart again with the same number; a kind with blend_s takes that long to come out of the kind before it, in colour, density and width, so the trail never changes at a cut (black, greying, the white puff, grey, the thin dark streak). soft: the strip's colour runs from piece to piece and its density swells with its width, so no piece shows as a block; it is lit across it, top and underside. A soft strip's piece is as dark as it will be from the moment it is laid (the trail's young end has drawn the smoke that far already), so no piece is pale at its near end for a frame and the trail never starts behind its engine. shadow, shadow_k: pale smoke's underside, away from the sun, and how far it goes to it. The widths are as seen: a strip thins to nothing at its sides, so tail_wide_m is set wider than the ruled width, which is where it is half as dark.

oil._what: an engine out and windmilling: heavy dark grey oil smoke, lumpy, one torn column, a thicker gout as the oil spits

streak._what: a fire put out and the airscrew feathered: a thin dark streak, about half the windmilling trail, that never clears

doused._what: the extinguisher going off in a burning nacelle: a white-grey puff for a second or two, then the streak

air_trails._mends_1952: Art director 19:52Z 20 November, on head ea8c1ba. tail_widen: past the tail a trail keeps widening, as its age over the time to the tail to this power (0.22: half as wide again by 100 m), a cone and never a tube. edge_torn: its two sides wobble in and out by this much more. fold: a lighter fold along inside it, the strip up to this much thinner on one side, the side wandering along it; never denser. knots: the share of its pieces that carry a soft lump of denser smoke, knot_r of the strip's half width across, knot_off of it off its middle, knot_alpha as dense and knot_dark as dark, for knot_s; one past 0.6 off the middle is the column's own colour and lumps its outline; three times as many in a gout, none when the room is four fifths full. oil's gout_s is short, so a gout is a lump seen running back down the trail. streak: dark from the nacelle; the game blends in linear light, where a dark thing over a pale sky loses about a third of its darkness on the picture, so alpha 0.75 reads 0.3 to 0.4 at the nacelle, paling to 0.6 of that by 60 m (0.15 on the picture). glycol: a cool grey underside 10 below a pale sky (shadow), and spurt_m: a denser, wider spurt that long behind the radiator, spurt_wide times the source's width and spurt_alpha as dense. fire: flame_tongues thin tongues a step in place of the one wide one, each rooted on the nacelle's skin round it, flame_over times past white at its root, licking back and flame_lift_of_length of its length off the skin at its tip.

funnel._what: a ship's funnel smoke (the art director's ruling of 05:30Z 21 November, art-director/explosions/funnel-smoke-ruling.md): round puffs laid by time into the air the ship steams through, never the air trail's strips
funnel._how: TrailStart(Now, Id, At, her velocity, "funnel", the funnel's width at its top in metres) and TrailMove every frame with her velocity and, last, the share of her top speed she is making (0 to 1; left out, her speed over top_speed_mps). A puff keeps none of her speed: it drifts with the world's wind and climbs, its height rise_k x root(funnel) x age^(2/3) / cube root(felt wind), so a fast ship's plume lies low and a stopped one's stands up (felt wind never under felt_least_mps). A puff is lip_of_funnel funnel widths across at the lip and widens by wide_k x funnel^wide_by_funnel x (metres of felt wind gone by)^(2/3). One is laid every 1/overlap of a puff's width. even (the art director, 14:13Z 21 November: no sky between the puffs): every other puff goes each time the plume has doubled its width, so the ones left always stand evenly; a puff thins as the plume deepens in them (the same smoke over more of them), and over the last even share of each such stretch the ones that go thin to nothing while those between take their smoke up. The first even_near halvings come at each doubling, the next even_far sooner (each when the plume is even_step times wider: far astern it is faint and needs fewer puffs deep), the rest at each doubling again. Without even: as they widen only as many hang on as still overlap that deep, by an even spread. size, shade: each puff that much bigger or smaller, lighter or darker; rough its lumpy rim, and heart_round 1 keeps its heart ring a true round under that rim, so the outline billows and the middle of the plume stays even. The plume rolls: a slow wave along it, one value every roll_run puffs at the lip and twice as far apart each time the plume has doubled its width, so a roll is always about as long as the plume is wide; where the wave is high the puffs ride roll_lift of their radius higher and are roll_shade darker, where it is low as much the other way (no lift at the lip, in full by three lip widths; never more than that, no dice). A wide funnel's puffs are laid closer: overlap_wide deep at wide_funnel_m across and wider, between funnel_m and that in proportion, each holding as much less smoke. full is the look at full_from of her power and over, cruise the look at cruise_to and under, blended between: alpha a puff's opacity at the lip, fallen by e at fade_s seconds old (as the power fade_pow of its age: over 1 it holds while young, then goes sooner); age_s how long the oldest hang; colour at the lip going to colour_old by old_by_s. surge: when her power rises by rise within about within_s she rings up, and for for_s the smoke is the surge look. shadow_of_lit, shadow_k: a puff's side away from the sun. lip_least_px: a far ship's puffs are never under that many pixels at the lip (at most lip_most times their size), so her plume is fewer, bigger puffs; and where the lip is far_px.0 pixels or under they overlap only overlap_far deep, each as much denser (in full from far_px.1). life_s is only the row's mark as a trail of its own.

fuel._what: a fuel tank alight, the flamer: long torn flame streaming back past the tail into dense black smoke

mist._what: fuel spraying from a torn wing root: a white mist torn back and gone in a second or two (it often catches: TrailStart again as fuel or fire)

air_trails._art_director_bremen: Art director's read of the air scene's Mac frames (a1acb552), 22 November, mend 2: the trails at Bremen were ropes, a core of 78 against a sky of 226, one width all along and crossing the whole frame. Wanted: 1-2 m at the source, 6-12 m by 10 s; opacity 0.9, 0.3 by 15 s, gone by 30 s; colour lifting from about 45 to 100-120 with age; edges breaking into puffs; no trail longer than about 2 km; an engine hit grey-brown, only burning fuel black and only near the aircraft. So smoke, fire, fuel and oil: widen to r1_m by widen_by_s 10 and on to thin_grow after; pale to pale_to 0.35 from 2 to 15 s and fade from thin_hold 0.5 of life_s 30; colour_old a light grey (smoke's grey-brown); lumps only from 0.8 of life, so the old end does not break into beads; edges torn (soft, edge_torn, wisps). longest_m 2400: a faster aircraft's trail is squeezed in time to that length of sky (about 2 km of it seen). Measured side-on at 80 m/s (smoke; fire): opacity 0.94, 0.88, 0.51, 0.33, 0.18, 0.06 at 0.5, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 s (0.94, 0.90, 0.54, 0.33, 0.19, 0.06), none at 30 s; colour 79 to 112 at 15 s (37 to 110); wide at half 1.3, 5.4, 8.7, 12.7 m at 0.5, 5, 10, 15 s (3.3, 8.0, 8.7, 10.7). At 150 m/s smoke 0.32 at 8 s, 0.12 at 12 s, gone by 16 s. Art director 08:54Z: the engine hit PASS; fire and fuel one step heavier, so a burning aircraft out-reads a damaged one: 12 m at 10 s and about 16 m at 15 s, opacity 0.75 at 10 s and 0.4 at 15 s, colour about 80 at 10 s, and the wake past the tail kept at 5 to 6 m (20 November). So fire and fuel r1_m 7 and 7.5, thin_grow 1.5, pale_to 0.56 from 5 to 15 s, thin_hold 0.4, colour_old 136,132,128, tail_wide_m 5 to 6. Fire measured: opacity 0.95, 0.96, 0.74, 0.41, 0.23, 0.08 at 0.5, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 s, none at 30; colour 39, 63, 87, 101, 109, 125; wide at half 4.0 m at 0.2 s, 11.4 at 5 s, 13.4 at 10 s, 15.4 at 15 s.

air_vapour.what: The owner's item 4 (26 November): white contrails at height that thicken as more aircraft pass. OFF until on is 1 (the air word -TheaterAirVapour lays battle-fx-air-vapour.json). The scene calls VapourMove each frame for each aircraft over the day's trail height. gap_spans: the clear gap behind the aircraft, in wingspans, before the trail forms. widen: metres across when laid, and by a damp sky's life. life_s: seconds a piece lives, a dry sky's and a damp sky's; persist: the cloud cover that is dry and that is damp (cover stands in for the humidity the game does not have). every_s: seconds between strips; far_every_s past far_from_m of the eye (fewer, longer pieces where no one can tell). near_m: within this of the eye, one strip behind each engine, closing into one over merge_s seconds; farther, one strip an aircraft. beyond_m: not drawn past this. most: pieces in the trails' own room, the oldest dropped first. colour and shade: its lit side and its side away from the sun (shade_k how much).

air_debris._how: A falling aircraft's debris row (AirFall once as the fall starts with its span and the deck height, AirFallMove every frame, AirFallStop when the model is gone). explode sheds fighter or bomber pieces at once (bomber at bomber_span_m or more), thrown throw_mps out and carried on at carry of its speed, with a short torn fireball; burn sheds burn_sheds over its fall, every_s apart, from first_s; spin sheds spin_sheds, the first a wing at wing_odds. A skin plate (plate_m across, painted face paint, bare metal inside bare) tumbles plate_tumble radians a second, so seen edge-on it thins and flutters, and glints when the sun catches it (glint, glint_power); it slows to sink at plate_sink_mps and drifts with the wind. A heavy piece (heavy_share of an explosion's, heavy_m, heavy_colour) drops at heavy_sink_mps. A wing (wing_chord_of_span) tumbles slowly down at wing_sink_mps. Every piece fades into the deck over its last enter_deck_m, at most most_s after it came loose; far off it shrinks to a speck under least_px and fades, never held up.
air_debris._art_director_0440: Art director 04:40Z (benchmark gap 3): a fall throws a debris row: 30 to 50 pieces for a fighter, 60 to 100 for a bomber; explode sheds them all at once, with a short torn fireball, never a ball; burn sheds 5 to 10 over its fall; spin sheds a few, sometimes a wing. Mostly light torn skin plates that flutter and glint, with a few heavy dark pieces that drop straight. Nothing pops out of view: falls and debris end in the cloud deck on a day with one, otherwise they keep falling until the haze or the ground takes them.

fireball._how: A short torn fireball, never a ball: lobes clumps of fire thrown out along tears ways at once, each r_of_span of the span across at birth, reaching reach_of_span, gone in life_s. Lit from within (art director 06:00Z): each clump is colour taken heart_mix of the way to hot_colour, cooling to deep_colour by cool_by_s and then gone into its smoke, near opaque to its edge (rim), its edge edge of the way to deep_colour so it reads as a lump of fire; rough its torn outline, drawn as two fans past twin_px. A white heart, broken in hearts pieces along the tears, each heart_r_of_span of the span across, heart_colour at its end, lasts heart_s and is drawn over the clumps. Each clump leaves smoke_colour smoke that grows smoke_grow times and hangs smoke_s at smoke_alpha, where the clump died, while the pieces fly on and fall; a lamp.
fireball._art_director_0600: Art director 06:00Z: pieces, smoke, falls and numbers PASS. Mend the fire's colour: it read as pale peach petals (median 222,165,130). Make it emissive: the heart near white-yellow (luma 240 or more) through about 0.1 s; the body a saturated orange (blue under about 60, saturation 0.75 or more); cooling to deep orange-red and the 140,40,16 edge by 0.2 to 0.3 s, then into the black smoke, never a clay or salmon tone on the way.

explode._how: An aircraft blowing apart (AirFall explode), the art director's ruling of 15:02Z 20 November (air-fates-look B). With this row the torn fireball is a ragged fire cloud across_fighter or across_bomber spans across by the fall's look, 0 to 3 (the event's; the kit throws no dice for it), bombs_across times that with bombs aboard and its white heart bombs_heart times as big and as long. Its clumps are thrown along the tears, each lobe_r of the cloud's half width at its end, and burn up to fire_s, cooling from orange to a dark ember brown (ember; its rim clump_edge; both written to land brown in the game's picture, no red) by one part in cool of that, whole until then and gone in a few frames after, the shortest out within a third of a second; heart_edge: the white heart is one hot core, each heart whiter, bigger and nearer the closer it lies to the middle (heart_fall) and falling off to heart_edge (heart_edge_in of the way at four tenths of its radius) at a ragged edge (heart_rough); black smoke boils out round each as it dies, swells to smoke_grow times the clump and hangs about hang_s by the look (its edge smoke_rough ragged), greying and drifting with the wind as a flak burst does. pieces: the debris row's count times this, by the look. streaks: how many clots of burning fuel fall out of it, by the look (bombs_streaks at least with bombs aboard): each (streak) is thrown throw_mps and carried on at carry of the aircraft's speed, is slowed by the air (drag, less than the cloud is, so it comes out of the cloud and curves all the way down) toward falling at sink_mps, and burns burns_s: an orange head head_m across burning over times past white and shrinking, flame torn off it along its path, and black smoke left along the whole path for smoke_s, laid in steps lengths. sparkle: how many winks of small metal catch the sun after it (air_debris.sparkle). Under air_debris.far_px of span on the screen, or with the room four fifths full, it keeps its flash, its fire and its smoke and throws nothing.

sparkle._how: Small metal catching the sun as it falls away from a break (the ruling: a sparkle for 1 to 3 s): each wink one point size_m across, never under least_px on the screen, burning over times past white for life_s, somewhere in the cloud of metal as it is carried on, spreads at spread_mps and sinks at sink_mps, at its own moment within for_s.

ways._how: The other ways down of the ruling (AirFall with the event's how). burst: small torn panels thrown at once as it starts (half as many again for a bomber, more by the look); sparkle: winks of metal (both more by the look); sparks: short bright streaks where two aircraft meet; sheds: more panels over the fall. The big pieces (a wing, the tail, an engine) are the model's own. pilot and glide throw nothing: their silence is their read. flamer and burn shed as a burning fall always has.

fuel_ball._how: Fuel going up (FuelBall): a ragged ball of burning fuel about the caller's Across metres wide, its time by its width (small_s at small_m across, big_s at big_m, in proportion between). Its lobes (lobes_per_m of its width, held to lobes), each burning life_share of its time and never going before its smoke can take it, are thrown out and up from a seat 0.3 of its half-width up, each to reach of its half-width and slowed by the air, lobe_r of its half-width at birth growing lobe_grow times; the whole climbs rise_of_across of its width while it burns, faster and faster, and each lobe rolls roll_rad_s as it climbs. Lit from within: each lobe colour taken heart_mix toward hot_colour, and heart_in more at the middle than at the rim, and up to deep_mix (more at the outside) toward edge_colour, so it billows; it holds that colour for cool_from of its life and then cools cool of the way to ember by its end; its rim edge of the way to edge_colour; the middle's lobes are sorted core_nearer of the half width nearer the eye, so from any side the hot middle shows through the cooler lobes round it; near opaque to its edge (rim), rough its torn outline, drawn as two fans past twin_px; the middle burns over times past white. hearts white-hot knots low in the middle for heart_s, heart_r of its half-width. Each lobe goes into black smoke_colour smoke at soot_life of its life (the first for a lobe at the ball's top, the second at its foot, so the dark comes in on top), never before smoke_from_s, born a little above it so the smoke boils off the top; with soot_in_s the smoke is whole that many seconds on and the lobe goes then, so none is seen fading over the sky. The smoke keeps smoke_climb of its lobe's climb (the first at the foot, the second at the top), growing smoke_grow times, climbing smoke_rise_mps, smoke_alpha thick, rough smoke_rough, ageing toward smoke_old and going as linger.fuel says; and from smoke_from_s top_puffs_per_m of its width more boil off its top as it climbs, keeping top_climb of the ball's climb, a black cap. The cloud by cap_s: each puff cap_spread further again out from the ball's upright, level with the ground; any whose top would pass the ceiling (the ball's middle as it went to smoke, cap_top of its half width over that) held cap_flat of that lower, and what stood above the ball's middle carried cap_raise of the way up under it, more the further out, so it is a cap with a flat top and level shoulders; leaning lean_deg down the wind by its height in a wind of lean_full_mps or more. stem_puffs_per_m of its width climb from the seat from smoke_from_s to stem_s, each to its own height up to the ball's middle as it went to smoke, stem_r of its half width widening stem_grow, so a dark stem stands down to the ground. A lamp of lamp times the root of its width, reaching lamp_reach of its width, up as it swells and down as it goes. Every piece of it keeps lens_near_of_across of its width as its own game.lens_cap near_m, so a lens caught inside it dims and never goes black. Without this row: nothing.
fuel_ball._ruling: Art director 21 November, section 2: rolling fireballs only from fuel: a vehicle 6 to 10 m for 1 to 1.5 s, an aircraft crash or a fuel dump 15 to 25 m for 1.5 to 2 s; black smoke from its top after 0.5 s. Fire as the air fireball's (06:00Z 20 November): heart near white-yellow, body saturated orange (blue under 60), cooling to deep orange-red and into the black smoke, never peach or salmon.
fuel_ball._mends: Art director 08:08Z 22 November on head D: sizes, times, the 0.1 s heart, the climb with its stem and the smoke boiling off the top from 0.5 s passed. 1. Lit hotter, the brightest thing in the frame (it read as popcorn: flat mid orange lumps each with a dark outline): the middle luma 190-220 about 255,190,80 through 0.5 s, down to an orange 150-170 by 1.0 s, the outer lumps 140-170, dark lacing only where soot forms, on top after 0.5 s, and never peach. 2. The big one's smoke too round: by 3 s a flatter top, 1.5-2 times the ball across, leaning 20-30 degrees down the wind, torn edges, a dark stem down to the fire on the ground, thinning as it goes. 3. The drama kept; the camera keeps twice the ball's width off it (its own thread) and the frame never goes black (lens_near_of_across).

vehicles._how: Mediterranean set 03:35Z and art director 06:19Z: every vehicle moving on dry ground trails dust from its dust sockets (dust.left, dust.right; VehicleDust every frame). Pale fine dust, the ground's own colour where it is thrown up (low) going paler as it climbs (high); low and long, drifting on the one wind (SetWind), lingering, never popping; taller and longer at speed (flatten, r1_m to r1_fast_m, life_s to life_fast_s between least_mps and full_mps); tracks throw tracked times more than wheels. A puff every spacing_m (no more than most_a_second); dense for haze_by_s, then a thin haze to its end. by_ground scales it; a ground not listed throws none. Pass check: from a 1.7 m eye a column's dust hides the vehicles behind its lead.
vehicles.when: dry ground and roads, not snow, mud or wet weather
vehicles._colour: Sand: the stony gravel 170,140,106 where it is thrown up (Mediterranean 03:35Z), losing colour as it climbs to a pale buff grey 210,196,170 (sat 0.2, art director 06:48Z) so the top reads as haze in the air, never a second layer of sand. Other grounds: their paint.dust, and colour_from_ground times it in the air.
vehicles._most_of_room: pre-check 07:10Z: the dust's gate takes the fuller of the whole room and the dust's own share of it (most_of_room), so dust alone never cuts a salvo behind the columns; a vehicle within full_within_m of the eye keeps its whole trail

low_skirt._how: Of every puff, share is a low dense skirt (flatten, wider by wide, thicker by thick): the trail's body, thick from the ground to a vehicle's height so what drives in it is hidden; the rest are the soft tall billows.

from_above._how: Art director 06:48Z: a player always finds his own units from above. On the overview, or any eye more than above_m up looking steeply down (the sine of its look down past steep), the dust within near_m of a vehicle laying dust, or of a gun its veil came from, thins to keep of itself, so each unit shows at least half; the long trail behind stays, a column's tell. Ground and follow eyes keep the full veil. No effect covers a unit's marker or banner: those are drawn over the effects.

men_going_down.puff: a small low puff at each man who throws himself flat

sound._how: The sound side lives in sound/mix/mix.json (impacts, flashToBang, big, shellShock). Effects and sound share one clock: the flash shows at once; the bang comes distance / 343 s later past 150 m.

never: a smooth ball, egg, dome or cotton wool, in smoke, dust or fire
a big orange fireball on a ground hit
peach; a flat orange smear painted on a surface
flat cards showing their edges, or a sprite turned square to the camera so it reads as a picture
smoke that vanishes in seconds; a crater that disappears
a white-out: the flash lifts the scene, never bleaches it

from_shell_cal._how: The land field battle's 'shell' event names a calibre (unreal/TheaterCommand/Rules/battle-bridge.ts, Explosions); this is the size row each one draws. A hit on armour (armour: true) draws on_armour at that size and leaves no crater. The event's ground is already one of the grounds keys.

ap_miss._how: An armour-piercing round that misses and strikes the ground: a single low spurt of earth and a skip, no crown, no crater (art director 16:53Z).

game._how: Numbers only the 3D game's effects kit uses (Source/TheaterCommand/Effects). Tune here, not in code.
game._max_puffs: The room: how many fans the kit lays in a frame at the most. Held to 100 to 20,000, and a value that is not a number gives 3,000 (the pre-check, 12:57Z: unchecked, a broken file's nan was a fault and its 1e9 asked for hundreds of gigabytes).
game._lumps_cost: The lumps' cost held (the builder's rested reading of build 1770, 15:09Z 20 November: Pearl Harbor 55.8 frames a second against 72.7 on 1766 and Midway 59.0 against 67.8 once the ships burned, every puff over its lumps_px carrying five lumps, each a fan of its own; the art director, 14:50Z: bound them to the biggest few dozen puffs as long as Midway 06 holds, and lumps faded to nothing must cost nothing). lumps_most: no more puffs than this carry lumps at once. With more wide enough, the places go to the widest on the screen and the rest stay plain; the width asked follows the count by half its size a second at most, and each puff's lumps come in over the next quarter of it, so none appears or goes at a stroke. Akagi's column in Midway 06 has about 40 such puffs and is laid exactly as passed; at 20 its lower half went smooth again. lumps_px_most: a puff wider on the screen than the first number counts for less the wider it is and loses its lumps by the second (window pixels). A column the eye is in or under fills the screen with such pieces: their lumps are murk, and cost the most of all to paint. lumps_least_ink: lumps thinner than this (0 to 1) are not laid at all. Without these three keys every lump is laid as in build 1770.
game._lumps_soft: The pre-check on 7d83869, 16:14Z 20 November: no single lump popped, but at the cap every lump in the fade band stepped together about once a second, 6 to 13% of all the lumps' ink in one frame, and blinked twice on a slow approach. lumps_soft_s: the width asked closes most of the way to the count's in this many seconds, the same at any frame rate, so a small move of the count is a fade over many frames (its tried cure: the biggest frame change 2% from 12%, no blinks). 0 or no key: at once, as 7d83869. Under the cap nothing changes: Midway 06 is laid exactly as passed. Not set here: lumps_band, the share of the width asked over which a puff's lumps come in (0.25 without the key). With many puffs alike in size most of the kept ones lie inside that quarter and show at under half strength (the pre-check's note); 0.15 gives the kept lumps a third more ink at the cap, but it also quickens every young puff's lumps under the cap, so Midway 06 would no longer be the picture passed.
game._steady_lamps: With fire.lamp.ramp_s: how many of the lamps (max_lamps) go first to the steadiest fires, the rest to the flashes of the moment and then the other fires. 1: a burning wreck's light stays put while gun flashes still light their own moment.
game._lamp: A flash's lamp at full strength (a 105 mm is 1), in candelas at 100 world units a metre (the kit scales it for other scales). 400 PASSED in build 1690 (art director 21:16Z): 1.23x screen brightness at 3 m and 1.11 to 1.15x at 13 to 16 m by night; 1200 overlit (1.57x).
game._muzzle_lamp: A gun's muzzle lamp (muzzles.<gun>.light_w) hangs this high times the square root of its strength above the muzzle, and its strength is cut by the square of how much lower that is than a shell's lamp of the same strength (burst.flash.light.height_m), so the ground at the gun's foot is lifted no more than at a shell's foot, never washed white. Build 1700: with the lamp at the muzzle, a tank gun at night lit the ground 1 m round its foot to 112 to 249 of 255.
game._shade: puffs are unlit: each is lightened toward the sun and darkened away from it by these shares, so a cloud has a lit and a shadowed side
game._backlight: Art director 22:24Z (dusk salvo sheet): with the sun behind, smoke never falls below about a fifth of the ground's value, from sky fill, and its thin edges and tips glow warm where the sun shows through, so it reads as smoke against the light and not as a hole. sky_fill: a smoke puff's shadow side is never darker than this share of its own colour in the hour's light. sun_through: the warm light added at a puff's thin edge when the eye looks toward the sun (sun_through_colour times the sun's own light, View::SunLight, white by day and none at night), falling off as the cosine to the sun to the power sun_through_power. Smoke clouds and trails only, most at middle thickness (art director 22:36Z): a low sheet of dust along the ground takes none, so it never glows as a fog over the field.
game._near_eye: Art director 17:52Z: smoke and dust one can see through fades out as it comes up to the camera, so it never fills the whole frame evenly (a barrage's dust drifting downwind over the eye was a flat beige sheet for about 4 s). near_eye_fade_m: nothing of a piece whose near edge is within the first of these of the eye, all of it from the second on. Never a light, a thrown clod, an aircraft's trail or an oil fire's column. At 2 and 8 the passed bursts at the battle camera (18.75 m off) do not change: a 105's nearest puff edge is 8.4 m off; a mortar's and a 75's nearest drifting puffs (5.7 and 6.3 m) thin by a third at most. Absent: no fade.
game._trail_near_eye: Art director 04:17Z 22 November, on the air scene's ride and chase cameras (build 2b177386): a trail passing the lens was a wide soft grey band across the frame or a black ribbon, and a strip through the camera's own plane a hard-edged sheet. trail_near_eye_fade_m: by its distance, nothing of an aircraft's smoke trail within the first of these of the camera and all of it from the second on, fading smoothly between. By how far the trail's line is from the camera, each end of a strip by its own, so the strip fades along its length with no step at a join. The art director's first numbers were 30 and 60, then 20 and 45 (04:43Z) so that the 60 m rear quarter film shot's fire trail does not thin toward its corner. That trail passes 39 m from that camera, so the second number is 38 and the shot is as it was (no pixel moves by more than 4 of 255; at 45 it still thinned by up to 54). trail_near_eye_looms: nearer than the second distance a trail still shows while it is small in the picture: all of it while its half width is under the first of these as a share of its distance from the camera, none of it from the second. So the aircraft the camera rides with still trails its smoke from the engine (thin there, and some 20 m off) and loses it as it widens toward the lens, and a wide old trail goes as it comes up to the lens. Without this key the distance alone decides and a ridden aircraft shows no smoke. trail_near_eye_least_m: however small in the picture, none of a trail within the first of these of the camera and no more than the distance leaves until the second, so nothing is drawn at the lens or through the camera's own plane. Flames are lights and stay. A ship's funnel smoke, a burst's smoke and gun smoke go by near_eye_fade_m. Absent: no fade.
game._trail_cut: The pre-check on 13388a4f, 22 November: an aircraft that speeds up (80 to 220 m/s and back) squeezes its trail row's life shorter, so the first piece laid fast ended before the slow pieces laid just behind it, and the trail had a hole up to 3.6 km wide for over 10 s. Now each piece laid before the squeeze rose is cut to end with that first fast piece (never later than its own end), so the trail always dies from its old end. A cut piece fades out over these last seconds before its cut (0.05 to 60; not a number gives 3). At a steady speed nothing is cut and every frame is as before.
game._sides: Points round each puff's ring (6 to 24). 12, so no eight-sided edge shows on a large near puff (art director 19:36Z asked 12 to 16). Each puff is 2 x sides + 1 points: 16 is rounder still if the Mac's frame time allows; 8 was the old shape.
game._shade_1936: shade_lit raised from 0.18 to 0.32 (art director 19:36Z): the sunward side of earth smoke shows as lit brown-grey; the shadow side stays charcoal (shade_dark 0.28).
game._day: How much the hour is day, from the light handed to Tick (its luminance): 0 at or below day_light_from, 1 at day_light_full. The campaign map's deepest night is about 0.377 (pre-check 21:16Z), so night is 0 there. By day (art director 21:16Z, build 1690) a lamp is day_lamp_share as strong and warm white (day_lamp_colour), and small guns (machine guns, rifles, guns under 75 mm, tank muzzles, aircraft guns and hits) light no ground at all; dust skirts stay. Tracer day widening reads the same Day.
game._lamp_frames: Art director 21:16Z, build 1690: a lamp never comes before its flash. A flash's lamp is full on the first frame drawn after the flash is born, about half on the next, then out. A light shorter than a frame (a flash, a flicker, a close tracer) is kept until a frame has drawn it once, so 30 frames a second and less still see every one.

lens_cap._how: The near-lens cap (the art director 22:46Z 21 November: clods faded 4 to 8 m from the lens, no card over 15% of the frame, no flash or flame over 20%, never a blackout; the ground scene's cut 4, still 06: a clod a few metres in front of the lens hung in the picture as a flat black slab). A thrown clod fades out from thrown_whole_m in front of the lens and is gone by thrown_gone_m; a smoke or dust card wider than card_most of the picture, or a flash or flame wider than light_most, fades away over the last soft of that, but only nearer the lens than near_m (by degrees over its last three tenths), so a column filling the picture from further off is never touched. Without thrown_whole_m, card_most and light_most: none, as before.
lens_cap._backstop: The art director 07:22Z 22 November: the camera keeps out of a burst's cloud for its first 4 s (about 30 m for a 500 lb bomb); as a backstop a size's own lens_near_m (sizes.<size>.lens_near_m: 75 mm 10, 105 12, 150 17, 250 lb 23, 500 lb 30) stands for near_m for that burst's pieces where it is more, so a lens caught inside a big cloud dims and never goes black.

soft_contact._how: The land battle's soft contact (the art director's cut 5, still 07, 22 November: a burning wreck's flame cut along a hard straight line where it met the hull; ruling 14:16Z, B). With the scene's FBattleEffects::SetSoftContact(metres) its material (M_BattlePuffsSoft) fades every piece where it comes within that depth in front of the ground or a hull, so a flame or smoke meets them softly. A piece lying on the ground would fade with it: a thrown clod or fragment come to rest, a spent case, a crater's mark. So each is laid lie_nearer times that depth nearer the eye along its own line of sight and smaller to match, the same picture to the pixel, every point of it that far in front of what it lies on: it stays whole, from any height of eye (a lift straight up would not: from above, 3 cm is 3 cm of depth; along the line of sight it is the full depth). Within four times that of the eye it is laid where it is. Off unless the scene calls it; the air and sea scenes never do.

smoke_budget._how: FX9 of the production lead's battle-scale plan (22 November): a budget for the screen's area of smoke, pre-built and OFF at first; on 1 since 22 November 21:45Z with thin 0, so only the skip of tiny pieces works (Brian's order of 21:20Z, smooth play first; the art director allowed the skip alone at 17:43Z and refused the thinning). on 0 is the old way. on 1: a piece of smoke (a burst's or a fire's puff or low skirt; not a light, a kept or oil column, a trail, a thrown piece, a far form or a funnel's even plume) under skip_px.0 across at its biggest takes no place and is not laid, coming in by degrees to whole at skip_px.1. And past screens of the smoke's fill a frame (each piece's area on the screen, over the screen's), the big smoke near the lens, over thin_from_px across (whole at a quarter as wide again), is thinned: a share of its pieces left out, each by its own lot and fading out over thin_band of lots, and the rest that much darker (the light they let through, to the power of one over the share kept), so a cloud of many keeps its weight. That share is what would bring this frame within screens, never over thin_most, followed over thin_s seconds so the smoke thins and comes back by degrees. The cloud rig (a 1.5 km front, 6 shells a second): the wide shot, 810 m back, fills 0.6 screens; the battle camera 150 m back fills 3.0, 1.7 of it 61 puffs over 200 px. The thinning has its own switch, thin (1 with on 1): the art director refused it at 17:43Z 22 November (the near veil tears into clear patches and dark lumps where one smooth body is the film look; if fill is ever proved to cost, try a lower-resolution smoke pass first, or merge near puffs into fewer, bigger, softer ones, never holes and lumps). The skip alone (on 1, thin 0) is invisible, and art has no objection to it. No row, or on 0: as before.

six_sided._how: FX7 of the production lead's battle-scale plan (22 November), pre-built and OFF at first; ON since 22 November 21:45Z (Brian's order of 21:20Z, smooth play first; the art director passed the look at 17:55Z). on 0 is the old way. on 1: a piece under under_px across on the screen (its long way) has its ring worked out at six of its points (the first, the one half way round where a piece's point and tail are, and four between, each the ring's nearest to a sixth of the way round), and every other point is a copy of the nearest of those, so the mesh stays as it is and the triangles between two copies cover nothing. At under 8 px the six sides lie within half a pixel of the round. Not a strip's piece, a tapered tracer, a squared case, a hub's fan, a tube or a round column's lump. No row, or on 0: as before.

room_shares._how: FX5, room shares by kind (production lead's battle-scale plan; built 11-22; ON since 22 November 21:45Z, Brian's order of 21:20Z, smooth play first; the art director passed the look at 18:30Z; on 0 is the old way). On, every gate but the vehicles' dust (bursts, their lingering smoke's slow fade, fires, trails, gun smoke) counts the room without the dust trails' pieces, up to dust.vehicles.most_of_room, so a column of tanks never thins them. The art director's ruling of 18:12Z: the dust trails give way first, by distance, in fewer, longer, softer pieces, never gaps or beads, and never stopped. The far trails are laid one puff in ShareThin of their own, each reaching back over the gap and as much denser, a little softer and wider; ShareThin rises while the dust holds more than the rest leaves it (dust_top of the room less the highest the rest asked over dust_memory_s, never under dust_floor of it) and falls when it holds less, over dust_thin_s, up to dust_most_thin. A vehicle within dust_full_m of the eye keeps its whole trail; thinning reaches full 2.5 times that far. No trail is thinned below dust_least_alive puffs alive along it. Far off, a vehicle's two dust sockets (Id 2K and 2K+1, as the land battle calls them) become one wider trail. Art director 18:31Z, PASS, and for the heaviest barrage until FX8: when thinning is not enough, far trails past dust_full_m are let go before any far burst loses a piece, the farthest first: once the rest's peak over dust_memory_s with the dust passes drop_from of the room, more go over dust_thin_s; under drop_back they come back. A trail let go lays nothing for at least drop_hold_s and what it laid fades over its own life, never cut; it comes back from its next puff, fading in. Cloud rig (sand, 120 tanks, 1.5 km front, battle camera 810 m back): the slow fade is whole at every rate; far bursts lose at most about 1% at 2 to 3.5 shells a second, and at 6 the far trails are let go and far bursts are as today (what they lose there is the bursts' own overflow, FX8's).

air_far._how: The air scene's far forms (its 11-22 ask, so its trail room can go from 24 to 60 at 150 aircraft); OFF until the air scene and the art director take them. trails_on: a trail past trails_from_m is laid as about trails_puffs puffs over its length, each that much farther apart and reaching back to the last as much farther, its hanging bars one in trails_keep_one_in of those puffs, so it is the same line in fewer, longer pieces; it goes over by degrees across the last trails_band of the range, so no length of a trail switches form, and nothing laid changes as the eye closes in. The art director's mends of 18:44Z: until the bar over them is laid, a far trail's short pieces stand in for it, as dark as the two would be together, so the smoke behind a far aircraft is never pale; each bar comes into sight point by point along it by the age there; and every far piece's sides swell and pinch by up to trails_billow of its width at each point along it (and a little more each side on its own), so a far trail billows and its edges are broken, never a smooth contrail. guns_on: a gun past guns_from_m flies no rounds; every guns_dash_s it lays one solid dash in its tracer core's colour along the aim, guns_dash_flight_s of a round's flight long, as wide as the far tracer's dash, carried with the aircraft; it takes up its rounds again where the dashes leave off. Cloud rig (five burning aircraft, 0.8 to 2.2 km, 60 m/s, guns in bursts): a far trail holds about 35 to 40 pieces against about 128, as dark all along as today's (averaged over five moments, within a few levels), with no jump frame to frame; a far gun lays a quarter of the pieces.

from_above._how: The art director's read of the general's stills (art-director/battles/general-cf671cb9, item 5, 22 November): seen from above at the general's height, 300 m and up, smoke was a flat dark smudge; she asked for a lit top, a pale side toward the sun, and its shadow laid on the ground downwind. Only for a scene that asks (FBattleEffects::SetFromAbove, the land battle), and only as its eye climbs from eye_m[0] to eye_m[1] over the ground and looks down from steep[0] to steep[1] (the sine of the angle down): a low eye sees nothing changed, as she ruled. Lit: smoke's face toward the sun goes up to lit of the way to lit_colour, most on each puff's sunward side and on its cloud's; black smoke (its own colour's light under dark_lum[0], going over by dark_lum[1]) only dark_lit of the way to dark_lit_colour, a warm brown-grey, as black smoke never goes pale in the sun, and every burning wreck's or oil fire's column, black smoke all, lit as a round column, takes dark_lit toward dark_lit_colour on its top by the sun's height (all of it from a sun 45 degrees up), all of it on its sunward side and a little over half on the far side, fading with each puff's edge, its young smoke over the fire less, so its root stays black (the art director's 19:59Z mend); none against the sun, nor at night, and never darker than it was. Shadow: one puff in shadow_every of the smoke at least shadow_least_r_m across and shadow_least_m over the ground lays its shadow where the sun's line through it meets the ground, shadow_colour at shadow of its own opacity, shadow_wide as wide, drawn out along the sun's way by the sun's height (at most shadow_stretch_most), following its puff as it drifts, grows and thins; the higher its puff the softer and wider its edge, fully so by shadow_soft_m; where shadows lie over each other the ground keeps at least 1 - shadow_darkest of its light, so a wide plume's shadow never stacks into a dark puddle (her 19:59Z mend); at most shadow_most of them, and never more than an eighth of the room. None with the sun under about 9 degrees. Off: on 0. Off (on 0) until the art director passes the game's stills and the Mac's frame rate holds 45 (production lead 23:10Z); the Mac flips it at launch with -TheaterFxSet=game.from_above.on=1, on a land battle that calls SetFromAbove(true).

air_flak._how: A flak shell bursting at the bombers' height (AirFlak). Five to eight see-through lobes in a crooked chain about long_m along the wind and across_m across it, each lobe_r of half the length, growing grow times; its two ends draw apart along the wind at stretch_mps for each half length out, and the whole drifts downwind at downwind_mps on top of the wind. Three to five thin wisps trail downwind. Opacity falls to half by half_by_s, then fades out; each piece lives life_s. Colour greys from colour to colour_old; cloud_shade lights its sunward side and shadows the far side, as the ground smoke. The lobes also spread across and up at spread_mps, their dark heart thins to heart_end of its middle as they age, and far off each lobe is held at least least_px across and made thinner to match. The flash: a torn orange glow gone in flash_glow_s with flash_spikes short bright spikes thrown out, and a white-hot heart in a hotter orange, a third to half the glow's radius off its middle, gone in flash_heart_s (radii in metres); off-centre and laid in front of the smoke; its lamp is lamp (a 105 is 1) reaching lamp_reach_m.
air_flak._art_director: Hanging-smoke brief, 2026-11-16 03:44Z, the look Brian picked ("its solid", "looks like a ball" of the first): smoke, never a body; uneven, torn, see-through at the edges, never round, softly shaded. Sizes from the brief's table in a B-17's wingspan (31.6 m): new 0.7 by 0.5 (22 by 16 m), 8 s 2.1 by 0.8 (66 by 25 m); heart opacity 0.96 new to 0.49 at 8 s; gone by about 9 s; drift about half a wingspan over its life. Flash about 0.2 s, no sparks: heart 255,245,215 about a tenth of a wingspan across, in 255,170,60, inside an orange glow 150,70,14 about half a wingspan across. Ruling 21:47Z: the clouds and colours PASS. Mends: the flash read as a ball (heart moved off the middle, the glow's edge torn at least 2 to 1 with two or three spikes, the glow gone in 0.1 s and the heart in 0.05 s); old bursts reach the full 2.7 times width and about 1.5 times height, lose their dark core first, and never shrink below about 12 px at range.

heavy._face_lit: Art director 23:44Z, first in-game flak: from above, against the fields, the burst read as an ink blot, in shadow all over. Smoke seen with the sun behind the eye shows its sunlit face: face_lit is how far a lobe then goes toward lit_colour (picture values), most on its outer lobes, wisps and sunward side, next to none in its young heart, none on its far side, which stays shadowed. Each lobe is laid as a dome: lit on the side toward the sun, its underside and edge darker. Art director 23:59Z: the lit faces must sit clearly above the field (about 135 to 150 in the game frame), so lit_colour is pale and face_lit over 1. Art director 00:03Z: never pale card: each puff at least twin_px across on the screen is two fans turned half a step (no facets; it takes two slots), the pale fades with the puff's own edge opacity (the rim goes see-through grey), and each lobe takes its own share of face_lit, 0.6 to 1.0, so the lit side breaks into lumps. Facing the sun and at night it keeps the dark look the art director passed; with the sun to the side or partly behind the eye (as her passed sky view, where the sun is partly behind) it is partly lit.

oil_fires._how: Art director's grit direction (19 November): ships burn black oil smoke; 2 to 4 dark columns on the horizon. Pearl Harbor and Midway mornings were mostly clear, so their grit is this smoke. One fire to each ship lost in a sea battle (the zone's kind: sunk = the oil burning where she went down, burning = where she left the line on fire), fixed where it is, to the fight's end, with the scene's one wind for every column. Its column is kept when the screen is full (keep), so a far column never blinks out.

sunk._rule: a slick of burning oil on the sea: low ragged flames on a few heads of the slick, and over them one fat black column standing up from the water, bending over down the wind as it climbs and cools, browner and thinner aloft
sunk._mend_0359: Art director 03:59Z: never close the top: from about 60% of its height it bends over and runs nearly level down the wind as a widening, flattening pall 2 to 3 times the column's height long, thinning to nothing (pall_*; the push burst_mps / burst_drag sets the height it levels at). It reads round: its sunward side lit to about 90 to 110 luma in a brown-grey, the shadow side kept at 24 to 35 (sun_side, lit_colour, oil_fires.round_up: lit as a round column, its width measured each frame); against the sun the warm fringe on its own edge only. Its base a low dark roll as wide as the slick, hugging the water, with a broken line of low flames along it (slick_long, slick_wide, flame_odds, flame_point, base_flat).
sunk._lumps: Art director 10:57Z 20 November, build 1766's Midway ships picture: Akagi's column was the right shape and colour and read as a soft brown smear. The cause was the kit's own picture, not Unreal's upscaler: a column puff is 60 to 90 m across, 300 to 400 of the window's pixels from a kilometre, and one fan whose edge fades over two fifths of its radius, so at that size no lump has an outline (drawing the scene bigger did not help, as the fade is a share of the puff). A column puff at least lumps_px pixels across on the screen carries lumps smaller lumps on its face: their sizes dealt from lumps_r of its radius, one step of that range to each, so every puff has a big one, small ones and the sizes between and no two puffs the same pattern (art director 11:29Z); each set lumps_out of the way from its middle to where it would touch the puff's edge, lumps_alpha as thick as the puff, its heart ring at lumps_inner (a firmer edge than the puff's), lumps_light of its light from its own sunward side and lumps_rim of it kept at its rim, so the dark between two lumps lies on their shadow sides. They come in between lumps_px and a quarter as much again, turn with the puff, and melt into it before it begins to thin (whole for three quarters of hold of its life, gone by hold): young smoke low in the column billows, old smoke aloft is one soft mass. Each takes a place in game.max_puffs only while its puff is that big on the screen and that young, and only a place nothing else wants: the lumps are not counted when the room is shared out, they are whole while a tenth of game.max_puffs would still be free with them all laid, thinner as that goes and not laid once the room is full, so a crowded sky costs a near column its billows, smoothly, and nothing else. The room is judged by the most places asked of late, held two seconds and then let down a hundredth of the room a second, and what is shown falls no faster than a half a second (the pre-check, 12:56Z: judged by one frame's count, every lump flickered with the fires' flames once the room was in its last tenth); so the lumps come back slowly after a crowd, up to 12 seconds from nothing to whole. A cut clears that memory for the frame and the next (the eye over 50 m from where it was a frame ago, turned by over 0.6, or its view a quarter bigger or smaller), so a close-up cut out of a crowded view shows its lumps at once. At lumps_px 110 one lost carrier from a kilometre took 435 places and one from the harbour picture's 1.5 km as many, which six ships there could not afford; at 260 the carrier takes about 220 and a ship in the harbour picture about 15: nearly all her young puffs are under 260 pixels across there and draw as they were passed. The pall aloft and the black root have none. The pixels are the ones the kit is told: the air scene tells it the window's, the map the ones it draws.

burning._rule: a ship on fire leaving the line, as the sea battle's 'burning' zone marks it: fires on the water where she went (or on her deck, if the caller gives the deck's height) and one narrower black column, a little greyer than burning oil
burning._mend_0359: Art director 03:59Z: greyer than the sunk ship's column, its foot about 60 to 80 (colour, a small grey roll: base_*). Its top runs down the wind as the sunk one's does (pall_*).

ablaze._rule: fx-air r2 (art director, Midway 06): a ship burning afloat, the scene's OilFire kind 'ablaze' for a ship lost to fire (AirStage's How 'burn'). A burning carrier's smoke stood hundreds of metres to kilometres high and bent over with the wind: from her deck fires (no burning slick and no flames of its own: her deck Burns are the flames), a narrow root about her beam wide, climbing hard to 250 to 300 m and leaning down the wind as the push dies, then on up slowly as it drifts, a long leaning plume. Black and dense low, browner grey and thinner high (pale_up_m, pale_up_most, pale_up_pow, pale_up_colour, thin_up: by its height over the fire a puff goes that share of the way to pale_up_colour and thins), lit on its sun side (sun_side, lit_colour, going toward pale_up_lit as it pales). An older kit without the row draws it as sunk.

oil_fires._pall_rest: pall_rest (art director 18:28Z): a pall puff's middle is never lower than this share of its own radius above the sea (Bit::Rest; 1.3 covers its rough outline), so one that wanders down (pall_drift_mps) is never cut by the sea along a straight line when seen from the air. 0 or no key: as before.

steam._how: Steam from a ship's boiler or engine-room hit, or a vehicle's radiator (art director 14:39Z 20 November): 'white that rises fast and vanishes, beside black that stays'. A narrow cone (cone_deg), clear for gap_m at the mouth where dry steam is not yet seen, then white rags that evaporate within life_s; never a bank, never brown, no flash. It roars for the first roar of its time, then its length and speed sink together to least of what they were, a wisp that wavers (waver) and leans with the wind. reach_m is how far a vent across_m wide throws it (by_width: how strongly a narrower or wider vent's reach follows its width); rag, a rag's radius at its end as a share of how far it went; mouth, its width at the mouth as a share of the vent's; lance, the share of rags that carry a short dense length of jet at the mouth, lance_long times as long as wide, living lance_life_s, so the fast root is one white lance and never a string of beads. vent: deck vents, skylights, holes in her side. funnel: the escape pipes on the funnel's face as the safety valves lift, a tall plume straight up. surge: the steam where water hits a fire being put out (reach: its height as a share of the fire's width). No such row: Steam does nothing.

smoulder._how: Release 2: a burnt-out wreck smouldering (the scene's LandBurn, after her flames): grey wisps rising lazily from her hatches and grilles, leaning with the wind, for the rest of the battle; each call dies down over its own time and the next starts it a little stronger. Its own colour, never steam's white.

smoke._how: Release 2: a knocked-out tank smoking before (or without) a fire: thick grey-brown smoke pushed out of her engine grilles or a hatch, rolling up and darkening the air over her (the scene's LandBurn). Thicker and darker than smoulder; its own colour.

cook_off._how: Ammunition cooking off in a burning tank, a ship's gun mount or aircraft parked on a deck (art director 14:39Z 20 November): 'repeated small pops, and flame roaring from the hatches'. Each pop: a small flash by the flash rule (flash: its size for a hatch a metre wide), a grey-black puff out of the hatch, orange embers thrown ember_up_m up in short arcs and cooling to dull red, and by fragment_odds a dark fragment tumbling off. NEVER a glowing round streaking skyward: a cooked-off round is not fired, and it reads as fireworks. The jet: jet_tall_m tall from a hatch hatch_m wide (taller from a wider one by the root of its width), jet_wide of its height across at its widest and never narrower than the hatch, ragged tapering tongues by the fire rules, black smoke off its top; in two pulses by two_pulses, sinking to pulse_dip between them. The caller says how many pops, over how long, how long the jet burns and when it starts. No bodies. No such row: CookOff does nothing.

glance._how: An armour-piercing shot glancing off armour (art director 14:39Z 20 November): 'a spark spray thrown the way the shot glances, and a glowing shot streaking off at a new angle'. A small two-frame flash by the flash rule (flash: its size for a 75 mm shot); sparks in a cone_deg cone along the glance, white-yellow cooling to orange, falling, gone in spark_life_s; a very small grey puff of paint and metal dust for half a second; the shot red-orange, leaving lift_deg off the plate at shot_mps, seen for shot_s, slowing hard (shot_drag, each second), veering veer_deg off its line and wobbling wobble_m about it tumble_hz times a second as it tumbles, and kicking up a little of the ground's dust where it comes down in sight. No burst, no smoke. Art director 15:40Z on the first cut: the shot was a long straight laser line and the sparks an even fan. The shot is now only the path it covered in the last streak_s (the 1/30 s streak rule), a tail that tapers and dims behind a small hot head (shot_head), bending as the path does and shortening as it slows; the sparks' speeds are skewed by the power spark_uneven (most slow and short, a few fast and long) and one in five leaves late. Each ricochet throws its own dice (the place, the moment, the kit's seed and how many came before), so no two take the same angle, kink time or kink direction. most_shots: no more shots than this are followed at once; one past that has its flash, sparks and puff only. The bright gouge it leaves is the model's to show, not the kit's. Sizes go by the root of the calibre over 75 mm. No such row: Glance does nothing.
glance._most_a_frame: The pre-check on de54166, 17:51Z 20 November: a ricochet's cost is its call (off a deck one pushes some 345 pieces, 0.6 ms; a dozen in one frame took 7 ms). No more than most_a_frame shots begin to be followed at one moment; one past it keeps its flash, sparks and puff, and its shot is not drawn. Without the key: no such limit, as before.
glance._shot_from: The production lead's FX4: a glance off armour from a calibre under shot_from_mm (a rifle's or a machine gun's round; the ground battle sends them at 8 mm, 1,541 in Normandy) is its two-frame flash and its sparks, and nothing more: no lamp, no puff of paint and no glowing shot followed off, so it takes none of most_shots and most_a_frame. Its sparks are as a glance's always were for its calibre, read at 20 mm at the least (about half a 75 mm shell's in count, speed and size). With its shot, each such glance was about 500 pieces; now 32 (its flash's ragged pieces and 7 to 13 sparks), and ten a second along a tank's side stand at 95 pieces at the most, against 3,023. A calibre that is no number counts as a shell's. Without the key, every glance as before.

sea._how: A sea battle (its own FBattleEffects, UseSeaDistance): its gun actions are fought with the enemy line 5 to 15 km from the eye, so it draws out to draw_beyond_m, and what a far line is read by is held up on the screen there. flash: the flame of a gun's flash or a hit's is never under least_px and keeps keep of its strength; where the whole flash stands under glow_px across it is far: its flame turns hot of the way toward colour and burns over times white, and a soft glow of the flame's own colour is laid over it, glow_px across and glow_alpha thick, outliving it by glow_s (all of that at half glow_px and under, none at glow_px). column: a shell column's jets and fingers are never under least_px long (a splash under 50 m tall as much less as the root of its height), keeping keep. Near the eye each is bigger than its floor and nothing changes. gone_px: beyond air.draw_beyond_m, where nothing used to be drawn, a piece of smoke, dust or water under that many pixels across takes no place (lights, kept columns and pieces with a floor of their own are left alone): a hit on the far line is over a thousand pieces a metre across. hit: beyond that distance a shell's or bomb's smoke on a ship or the land is fewer, bigger puffs the smaller it stands: all of them where its crown is full_px tall, that share under it, never under least (coming in over the next over_m), and under half of them it has no skirt of dust.

linger._what: Smoke that fades gradually into the air (Brian, 18:00Z 21 November: 'have the smoke effects gradually fade away into the air not disappear right away'; the art director's ruling of 19:58Z, art-director/explosions/smoke-burst-fire-ruling-r2.md). Each kind's cloud is as thick as it was until thick_s after its burst, then goes over the time to gone_s: at half its thick opacity a third of the way, at a tenth by two thirds, under a twentieth for the last fifth, two to three times as wide by the end, climbing and drifting, and paling to the colour of the air behind it, never pink.
linger._how: keep: the share of the cloud's puffs that stay to the end and take over the smoke of the others, which retire over the first go_by of the tail. left_third and left_two_thirds: of the smoke the cloud had when thick, what is left a third and two thirds of the way from thick_s to gone_s (a deep cloud must lose most of its smoke before the eye sees it thin: tuned in the preview's pictures so the cloud reads half as strong and then a tenth there). wide: by the end a puff is that much wider again, its smoke thinner over the wider face. spread: and stands that much further again from the cloud's own middle, so the cloud is two to three times as wide. lift_mps: it climbs that much more. A puff's other looks (its own widening, colours, heart) keep the clock they had. Any of these numbers may be given for one size or gun under by.<name>. Between pale_from and pale_by of the way it goes 'pale' of the way to the sky the scene gave (SetSky; sky_share of it) or to 'to'. Remove a row, or its times, and that kind goes as it did before.
linger._spare: Short of room, a new cloud keeps fewer of its puffs to its end and the rest retire sooner, the ones that stay taking the smoke of the rest as ever: all of its keep and go_by while under spare_from of the room (game.max_puffs) is asked for, down to spare_least of them at spare_by. So a long barrage's old smoke never crowds out its new bursts.
linger._never_sooner: A cloud is gone no sooner than its longest puff was before this rule: its tail runs from thick_s to the later of gone_s and that, by the same curve (the pre-check on 86d71f2: a bomb's smoke lived 45 to 120 s by its size's linger_s, 1.6 times that on sand, and gone_s 45 and 60 cut it short).
linger._stay_low: A burst with bulk: a puff at the cloud's foot is stay_low the likelier to stay to the end than the cloud's share, and one at its top that much the less, so the base holds the smoke and thins last while the smoke above lifts (art director 20:50Z 21 November).

smoke_screen._why: The drill book's smoke screens (22 November): a smoke round makes no crater and no dark cloud. A phosphorus round (wp, the American 60 mm) bursts hard and white and throws burning streamers in a dome, each trailing white smoke that curls over as it falls; a burning bomb or canister (the British 2-inch, the others') gushes from where it lies. From either a low white wall is laid for as long as the round burns (the battle says: a light mortar's about 60 s and 18 m, an 81 mm's 90 s and 24 m, a field gun's 150 s and 30 m), its lumps swelling as they drift down the wind, so it is one screen through its middle with rags at its edges, thickening over build_s and thinning from thin_from of its time.

grenade._why: A tank commander's smoke grenade covering his crew's bail-out (release 2, -TheaterLandBailSmoke). Round 2 by the art director's notes of 24 November 02:18Z, Battle::GrenadeLumps: one short jet off the canister first (jet_*: small lumps hissing out down the wind, stopped by the air within jet_reach_m), never a puff and a dot; a dense rolling billow standing at the canister (billow_*: big lumps rolling over, carried off slowly); then a plume leaning down the wind, climbing rise_per_m metres a metre and widening tail_grow times, with torn wisps off its top and sides (wisp_*, laid as well as its body's lumps, wisp_share of its steps, so its body never gaps); each plume lump as thick as laid for solid_m metres of its way and then thinner by e every fade_m metres more (as the power fade_pow), so it is solid for the first 10 to 15 m and about a fifth as thick 40 to 60 m down, gone by plume_m; grey-white (grey of the way to the screen's shadow_colour), its top toward the sun lit shade_k and its underside and lee going lee_k of the way to lee_colour, so its sunlit top is about 215-230 and its underside 160-185 in the cloud pictures; resting on the ground (rest of its radius) until it climbs off; and a soft shadow on the ground under its dense part, laid away from the sun (shadow). It gushes at once (build_s), start_m across by 2 s, the caller's width at the canister by swell_s, and thins over its last thin_last_s. The wall's own pieces (wp, canister) are untouched.

sea_splash._why: A shell falling in the sea by its calibre, SeaSplash(At, CalibreMm, Dye): the art director's columns by calibre (sea-guns-ruling.md part 5, 06:12Z 21 November) on the passed column's build (grounds.water.spout), and the dye its ship loaded (historian/dye-loaded-shell-splashes.md, 22 November). The table runs by calibre_mm, each number between the two calibres either side and held at its ends: height_m, the column's height (heavy 14 to 18 inch 50 to 70 m, medium 8 inch 25 to 35, light 5 to 6 inch 12 to 20); rise_s, about its full height by then; hang_s, it stands near that height so long; fall_s, then it falls as a curtain and is back on the sea, its top the last down; foam_m and foam_s, the patch it leaves, across and how long; crown_wide, its head's half width for its height (a light one a short bushy plume). mist_s: the fine spray at its foot hangs about so long (4 to 6 s at a heavy column's, less by the root of the height). foot_white: as it stands its foot is broken at least that far to white water, so the dark wet water is the first moment's and never a dark lump under it for seconds (0: as the passed column). far_px: where the whole column stands under that many pixels tall in the last frame's picture (in full from half that down), its white water is written up to far_over past white so it stands over a pale sky (the ruling: lit side 20 over the sky) and its dark foot goes far_foot of the way to the column's shade colour, so it is never a small dark puff. Dyes: a name the scene passes for the firing ship (Nagato pink, Kongo red, Haruna yellow, Yamato none; the US heavy ships by the historian's table; British from late 1942; everyone else none, white): colour, its water in the sun, written to land; shade, its shade side; shift, what it turns toward against the sun or with the sun low, shift_k of the way (Kongo's red to purple); stain, the foam patch's tint, stain of the way; strength, 0 to 1. The column is dye_k of the way to the dye through its body, dye_top of that at its crown and dye_foot in the dark water at its foot, and pales dye_pale of the way back to white as it falls; its mist mist_dye. shake_within_k: a near miss jolts an eye within that many times its height. Without this row SeaSplash draws Shell on water with bomb500, bomb250 or how150 as the scene did.
