green._who: Wisconsin, North Carolina; Duke of York, Valiant

sea_screen._why: A smoke screen laid at sea by a ship under way, ScreenLay(Id, At, Velocity, bFunnel) every frame and ScreenLayStop(Id) (the sea scene's ask, 22 November: Samar's escorts laid 8 screens, up to 5 at once; the art director: each escort lays her own plume, dense at the source, white-grey from the stern generators and black from the funnels, lumpy, thinning downwind, with gaps). Not the land's smoke_screen (a smoke round's wall). Laid by time, as a funnel's plume: a puff every overlap-th of its width of the wind she feels (felt_least_mps at least), let go into the air with none of her speed; it rests on the water (rest: its middle at least that share of its radius up), climbs rise_mps, drifts with the wind, wanders across it (spread_mps) and is drawn out along its line (stretch). Its width is lip_m at her stern and grows by wide_k times its age to the two thirds; as it does, its puffs go by halves (even, even_near, even_far, even_step, as the funnel's), so the screen is unbroken and its old end costs few pieces, each holding its smoke over a face as much wider: it thins downwind. Each puff also thins by its age (fade_s, fade_pow) and is gone by age_s; along the screen some stretches (gaps, over gap_s of laying, past gap_from of a slow random value) thin sooner, and gap_thin of their smoke is thin from the start, so gaps open in its old parts while it stays dense at her stern. billow: that share of its puffs are billows, billow_size as big and climbing billow_rise as fast, so its top is heaped and uneven. Colour: colour, going to colour_old by old_by_s; its side from the sun shadow_of_lit of it, shadow_k of the way; size and shade, the dice on each puff; rough, lumps, lumps_px and the roll (roll_lift, roll_shade, roll_run) its lumps. white: the stern generators' chemical smoke. black: the funnels', born from_up_m higher and from_ahead_m forward of the stern the scene gives. Far off: least_px, no puff under that many pixels across at its birth in the last frame's picture (at most lip_most times its own width), overlapping overlap_far deep, each as much denser: fewer, bigger puffs. busy_from: past that share of the room (game.max_puffs) a screen lays half as deep. restart_after_s: a screen not called for that long starts afresh. most_a_call: puffs laid in one call at most.

far._how: The far form (BombStick; TheaterFxCore.h, FarLay). Beyond the scene's draw range (air.draw_beyond_m, 4 km) a bomb that lands is drawn as a few large soft pieces in place of its near burst's hundreds, out to draw_beyond_m: a flash held to least_px on the screen with a soft glow, so a stick's bombs ripple along the line; and the parts below, each a share of the size's cloud_m across (r: at birth and by grow_s, then late times that by its life's end), coloured from the ground's dark heavy earth (0) to its light smoke and dust (1) (paint: at birth and by settle_s; on water from the spout's base_colour to its white), never under least_px across, keeping keep of their opacity there. crown: the earth thrown up, tall times as high as wide, gone in life_s. body: the dense cloud of earth on the ground. veil: the lighter smoke that lifts and spreads. skirt: the low dust ring (upright: a low flat ball on the ground). On the sea: column (the white water standing up), foam, mist. A part that lingers goes as its size's near cloud does (linger.shell, never sooner than the size's linger_s), widening, lifting lift of the row's lift_mps and paling to the sky, and looks left_third and left_two_thirds as thick a third and two thirds through its tail (the art director's half and tenth, 19:58Z 21 November). A part that merges is laid once for as many bombs of a stick as stand within merge_px of each other on the screen, drawn out along the stick as its bombs land. Within the range the near burst is drawn, and its far form takes over across the last hand_over of the range; keep 1: far pieces are kept first when the screen is full. walk_mps: the bombers' speed over the ground, a stick's bombs landing that far apart in time when the caller gives none.

land_grade._how: The land battle grades its own picture (most of the colour out of the darks and the middles, contrast 1.42, half a stop down: tools/battle-fx/land_grade.py), not by the game's curve these colours are written for, so a scene under it says so (FBattleEffects::SetLandGrade) and this row stands in for what it names, each at the same path under land_grade. Art director on cut 5 (06, 22 November): the clods were flat black silhouettes, core L 9; lit as earth they are about 45 to 70 in the smoke's shade, brown about 70,58,45, lumps not cards. Written with land_grade.py write: earth 118,103,61 lands 72,62,42 (art director 14:09Z: earth, not rose-brown; first 118,99,72 for 70,58,45 leaned rosy on the lit faces); mud 110,97,59, snow 125,114,76 and woods 138,118,67 the same lift over what they were painted to show, and sand's stones 107,93,53 (its clods land 72,59,45 already). The grade is steep (a tenth darker is ten levels darker), so the clods' shade (lit face and dark face) is 0.5 and their tint 0.95 to 1.05, holding a clod within about 40 to 80, and the shower's backlit undersides 0.9 to 1.0 (45 to 60) where 0.55 went black. Art director 13:58Z: the yellow tracer written for the grade lands near 214,207,103 (with the fire's spread 220,207,118; plain, it landed pale khaki 202,197,162 and was lost in the wheat): colour 232,208,0, and by day its edge 255,178,0 (233,193,110 with the spread, aim 229,196,31). Its white-hot core stays as it is. The desert (the production lead's theatre ask, 17:46Z 22 November; the art director's 13:30Z rule, colours written warmer to land on her numbers): sand's soil, heavy jets, dust and smoke, and the vehicles' sand dust low and high, written with land_grade.py write to land as grounds.sand.paint and dust.vehicles say the picture shows them (dust 196,174,135 was landing grey 185,174,154, smoke 160,144,126, heavy jets near black 38,31,21; vehicle dust 200,195,187). Sand's clods (72,59,45) and stones stay as passed, its foot black.

_targets._how: The colour each desert paint and dust must land at on screen, as the art director passed them (11-22). land_grade.py retarget <recipe> <grade> --apply writes every entry again for a ground's grade; _targets_grade names the grade the writes above were made for.

land_grade._desert_dust: Art director, 03:04Z 24 November (release 1.5, Sidi Barrani on 849c1bc1): the tank dust was mustard, 201,158,50, and read as a coloured smoke grenade; it should be the ground's colour, about 205,190,160 at the root, thinning. Two things put it there. The sand row above was written for Normandy's grade (_targets_grade), but the desert's recording carries its own (land_grade.py GRADES desert: middles 0.66, contrast 1.25, 0.6 stops down), under which the old low dust landed 168,131,83, deeper than its 170,140,106; and the fire's spread after the grade (M_FireSpread, on the land battle's lens since 22 November) takes any kit pixel of fire's hue, orange to yellow, deep in colour (saturation past 0.30) for fire and doubles its colour: 168,131,83 went to 200,149,32. The shells' paints on sand (soil, heavy jets, dust, smoke) were the same: Normandy-written, they landed after the desert's grade and the spread at 174,130,30, 119,85,14, 220,160,39 and 198,149,40, orange and mustard; written again the same way they land on the art director's passed 150,128,95, 96,78,55, 196,174,135 and 176,152,118. Sand's stones and clods stay as passed.
